verses.1:1: And Moab rebelled against Israel after the death of Ahab.
verses.1:2: Ahaziah fell through the latticework in his upper room in Samaria and grew ill. He sent messengers and said to them, "Go, inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, whether I will recover from this illness."
verses.1:3: But the angel of the LORD spoke to Elijah the Tishbite, "Get up, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and speak to them: 'Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron?
verses.1:4: Therefore this is what the LORD says: The bed onto which you have gone up, you will not come down from it, for you will certainly die.'" So Elijah went.
verses.1:5: The messengers returned to him, and he said to them, "Why is it that you have returned?"
verses.1:6: They said to him, "A man came up to meet us and said to us, 'Go, return to the king who sent you, and speak to him: This is what the LORD says, Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are sending to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron? Therefore, the bed onto which you have gone up, you will not come down from it, for you will certainly die.'"
verses.1:7: He spoke to them, "What was the appearance of the man who came up to meet you and spoke these words to you?"
verses.1:8: They said to him, "A hairy man, with a leather belt fastened around his waist." And he said, "That is Elijah the Tishbite."
verses.1:9: Then he sent to him a commander of fifty with his fifty. He went up to him, and there he was, sitting on top of the hill. He spoke to him, "Man of God, the king has spoken: Come down."
verses.1:10: Elijah answered and spoke to the commander of fifty, "Now if I am a man of God, may fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty." So fire came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty.
verses.1:11: Again he sent to him another commander of fifty with his fifty. And he spoke up and said to him, "Man of God, this is what the king says: Come down quickly."
verses.1:12: Elijah answered and spoke to them, "If I am a man of God, may fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty." So the fire of God came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty.
verses.1:13: Again he sent a third commander of fifty with his fifty. The third commander of fifty went up and came, knelt on his knees before Elijah, pleaded with him, and spoke to him, "Man of God, please let my life and the lives of these fifty servants of yours be precious in your sight.
verses.1:14: Look, fire came down from heaven and consumed the first two commanders of fifty and their fifties; so now let my life be precious in your sight."
verses.1:15: Then the angel of the LORD spoke to Elijah, "Go down with him; do not fear him." So he got up and went down with him to the king.
verses.1:16: And he spoke to him, "This is what the LORD says: Because you have sent messengers to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron—is it because there is no God in Israel to inquire of His word?—therefore, the bed onto which you have gone up, you will not come down from it, for you will certainly die."
verses.1:17: So he died according to the word of the LORD that Elijah had spoken, and Jehoram began to reign in his place in the second year of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, because he had no son.
verses.1:18: As for the rest of the deeds of Ahaziah that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.2:1: Now it happened, when the LORD was about to bring Elijah up to heaven in a whirlwind, that Elijah and Elisha went from Gilgal.
verses.2:2: Elijah said to Elisha, "Please stay here, because the LORD has sent me as far as Bethel." But Elisha said, "As the LORD lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." So they went down to Bethel.
verses.2:3: The sons of the prophets who were at Bethel came out to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today the LORD is taking your master from over your head?" He said, "I also know it; be silent."
verses.2:4: Elijah said to him, "Elisha, please stay here, because the LORD has sent me to Jericho." But he said, "As the LORD lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." So they came to Jericho.
verses.2:5: The sons of the prophets who were at Jericho drew near to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today the LORD is taking your master from over your head?" He said, "I also know it; be silent."
verses.2:6: Then Elijah said to him, "Please stay here, because the LORD has sent me to the Jordan." But he said, "As the LORD lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." So the two of them went on.
verses.2:7: Fifty men from the sons of the prophets went and stood across from them at a distance, while the two of them stood beside the Jordan.
verses.2:8: Elijah took his cloak, folded it up, and struck the water, and it divided to this side and that, so the two of them crossed over on dry ground.
verses.2:9: When they had crossed over, Elijah said to Elisha, "Ask what I may do for you before I am taken from you." Elisha said, "Please let a double share of your spirit come to me."
verses.2:10: He said, "You have asked a difficult thing. If you see me being taken from you, it will be so for you; but if not, it will not happen."
verses.2:11: As they kept walking along and talking, suddenly a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated the two of them, and Elijah went up in a whirlwind to heaven.
verses.2:12: Elisha was watching and crying out, "My father, my father, the chariot of Israel and its horsemen!" And he did not see him again. Then he seized his garments and tore them into two pieces.
verses.2:13: He picked up Elijah's cloak that had fallen from him, returned, and stood at the bank of the Jordan.
verses.2:14: Then he took Elijah's cloak that had fallen from him, struck the water, and said, "Where is the LORD, the God of Elijah?" When he too struck the water, it divided to this side and that, and Elisha crossed over.
verses.2:15: When the sons of the prophets who were at Jericho saw him from across the way, they said, "Elijah's spirit has come to rest on Elisha." And they came to meet him and bowed down to him to the ground.
verses.2:16: They said to him, "Look now, there are fifty strong men with your servants. Please let them go and search for your master; perhaps the Spirit of the LORD has lifted him up and cast him onto one of the mountains or into one of the valleys." But he said, "You must not send them."
verses.2:17: Yet they pressed him to the point of embarrassment, so he said, "Send them." So they sent fifty men, who searched for three days but did not find him.
verses.2:18: When they came back to him—he was staying in Jericho—he said to them, "Did I not tell you, 'Do not go'?"
verses.2:19: The men of the city said to Elisha, "Look now, the site of the city is good, just as my lord sees, but the water is bad and the land causes miscarriage."
verses.2:20: He said, "Get me a new bowl and put salt in it." And they brought it to him.
verses.2:21: Then he went out to the spring of the water, threw salt into it, and said, "This is what the LORD says: I have healed this water; no longer will there be death or miscarriage from it."
verses.2:22: So the water remained healed to this day, according to the word of Elisha that he spoke.
verses.2:23: From there he went up to Bethel. While he was going up along the road, young boys came out from the city, taunted him, and said to him, "Go up, baldhead! Go up, baldhead!"
verses.2:24: He turned around, saw them, and cursed them in the name of the LORD. Then two female bears came out of the forest and tore apart forty-two boys from among them.
verses.2:25: Then he traveled from there to Mount Carmel, and from there he went back to Samaria.
verses.3:1: Now Jehoram son of Ahab began to reign over Israel in Samaria in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, and he reigned for twelve years.
verses.3:2: He did evil in the eyes of the LORD, yet not like his father and his mother, because he removed the pillar of Baal that his father had made.
verses.3:3: Still, he held fast to the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, by which he caused Israel to sin; he did not turn away from them.
verses.3:4: Now Mesha, king of Moab, was a sheep breeder, and he regularly rendered to the king of Israel one hundred thousand lambs along with the wool of one hundred thousand rams.
verses.3:5: And it happened, at the death of Ahab, that the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
verses.3:6: So King Jehoram went out from Samaria on that day and mustered all Israel.
verses.3:7: He went and sent word to Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, saying, "The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me against Moab for battle?" He replied, "I will go up. As I am, so are you; my people are as your people, and my horses are as your horses."
verses.3:8: Then he asked, "By which way should we go up?" And he answered, "By the way of the wilderness of Edom."
verses.3:9: So the king of Israel, the king of Judah, and the king of Edom set out, and they circled around on a journey of seven days, and there was no water for the camp or for the animals that followed them.
verses.3:10: Then the king of Israel said, "Alas! The LORD has summoned these three kings to give them into the hand of Moab!"
verses.3:11: But Jehoshaphat asked, "Is there no prophet of the LORD here, so that we may inquire of the LORD through him?" One of the servants of the king of Israel answered and said, "Here is Elisha son of Shaphat, who poured water over Elijah's hands."
verses.3:12: Jehoshaphat said, "With him is the word of the LORD." Then the king of Israel, Jehoshaphat, and the king of Edom went down to him.
verses.3:13: Elisha said to the king of Israel, "What is there between me and you? Go to the prophets of your father and to the prophets of your mother." But the king of Israel said to him, "No, for the LORD has summoned these three kings to give them into the hand of Moab."
verses.3:14: Elisha said, "As the LORD of hosts lives, before whom I stand, if it were not that I honor the presence of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, I would neither look toward you nor see you.
verses.3:15: But now, get me a musician." And it happened, as the musician was playing, that the hand of the LORD came upon him.
verses.3:16: And he said, "This is what the LORD says: Make this streambed full of trenches.
verses.3:17: For this is what the LORD says: You will not see wind and you will not see rain, yet that streambed will be filled with water, and you will drink—you, your livestock, and your animals.
verses.3:18: And this is an easy thing in the eyes of the LORD; He will also give Moab into your hand.
verses.3:19: You will strike every fortified city and every select city, bring down every good tree, block up every spring of water, and ruin every good plot of land with stones."
verses.3:20: In the morning, at the time the offering was brought up, suddenly water came from the direction of Edom, and the land was filled with the water.
verses.3:21: Now all Moab heard that the kings had come up to fight against them, so all who could strap on armor and older were called to arms, and they stood at the border.
verses.3:22: When they got up early in the morning, the sun was shining upon the water, and from across the way Moab saw the water red like blood.
verses.3:23: They said, "This is blood! The kings have surely destroyed one another, and each has struck down his companion! Now then, to the plunder, Moab!"
verses.3:24: They came to the camp of Israel, and Israel rose up and struck Moab, so Moab fled before them; and Israel struck into it, continuing to strike Moab.
verses.3:25: They tore down the cities, and onto every good plot of land each man threw his stone and filled it; they blocked up every spring of water and brought down every good tree, until they left only its stones in Kir-hareseth. Then the slingers surrounded it and struck it.
verses.3:26: Seeing that the battle was too strong for him, the king of Moab took with him seven hundred men who drew the sword in order to break through to the king of Edom, but they could not.
verses.3:27: Then he took his firstborn son, who was to reign in his place, and offered him up as a burnt offering on the wall. And great wrath came upon Israel, so they withdrew from him and returned to the land.
verses.4:1: Now a woman from among the wives of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, saying, "Your servant, my husband, has died, and you know that your servant was one who feared the LORD; yet the creditor has come to take my two children for himself as slaves."
verses.4:2: Elisha said to her, "What should I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house?" And she said, "Your maidservant has nothing at all in the house except a flask of oil."
verses.4:3: Then he said, "Go, borrow vessels for yourself from outside, from all your neighbors—empty vessels; do not gather only a few.
verses.4:4: Then go inside and shut the door behind you and behind your sons, and pour into all these vessels; and set aside each one that is full."
verses.4:5: So she departed from him and shut the door behind her and behind her sons; they were bringing them to her, and she kept pouring.
verses.4:6: When the vessels were filled, she said to her son, "Bring me another vessel." And he said to her, "There is not another vessel." Then the oil stopped.
verses.4:7: Then she came and told the man of God. And he said, "Go, sell the oil and repay your debt, and you and your sons may live on what is left over."
verses.4:8: Now one day it happened that Elisha crossed over to Shunem, where there was a prominent woman, and she pressed him to eat bread. So it came about that whenever he passed by, he would turn aside there to eat bread.
verses.4:9: She said to her husband, "Look now, I know that he is a holy man of God who passes by us continually.
verses.4:10: Please let us make a small walled upper room and place there for him a bed, a table, a chair, and a lampstand; then when he comes to us, he can turn aside there."
verses.4:11: One day he came there, and he turned aside into the upper room and lay down there.
verses.4:12: Then he said to Gehazi his servant, "Call this Shunammite woman." So he called her, and she stood before him.
verses.4:13: And he said to him, "Please say to her, 'Look, you have cared for us with all this anxious care; what is to be done for you? Is there anything to be spoken on your behalf to the king or to the commander of the army?'" And she said, "I live in the midst of my own people."
verses.4:14: So he said, "Then what is to be done for her?" And Gehazi said, "Indeed, she has no son, and her husband is old."
verses.4:15: He said, "Call her." So he called her, and she stood in the doorway.
verses.4:16: Then he said, "At this appointed time, when the season comes round again, you will be embracing a son." And she said, "No, my lord, man of God, do not deceive your maidservant!"
verses.4:17: And the woman conceived and gave birth to a son at that appointed time, when the season came round again, as Elisha had spoken to her.
verses.4:18: The child grew, and one day he went out to his father, to the reapers.
verses.4:19: He said to his father, "My head, my head!" And he said to the servant, "Carry him to his mother."
verses.4:20: So he carried him and brought him to his mother, and he sat on her knees until noon, and then died.
verses.4:21: She went up and laid him on the bed of the man of God, shut the door behind him, and went out.
verses.4:22: Then she called to her husband and said, "Please send me one of the servants and one of the female donkeys, so that I may run to the man of God and return."
verses.4:23: He said, "Why are you going to him today? It is neither new moon nor Sabbath." And she said, "All is well."
verses.4:24: Then she saddled the female donkey and said to her servant, "Drive on and go; do not hold back my riding unless I tell you."
verses.4:25: So she went and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her at a distance, he said to Gehazi his servant, "Look, there is that Shunammite woman!
verses.4:26: Now please run to meet her and say to her, 'Is all well with you? Is all well with your husband? Is all well with the child?'" And she said, "All is well."
verses.4:27: When she came to the man of God at the mountain, she grasped his feet. Gehazi came near to push her away, but the man of God said, "Leave her alone, for her soul is bitter within her, and the LORD has concealed it from me and has not told me."
verses.4:28: Then she said, "Did I ask for a son from my lord? Did I not say, 'Do not mislead me'?"
verses.4:29: Then he said to Gehazi, "Belt your waist, take my staff in your hand, and go. If you meet anyone, do not greet him, and if anyone greets you, do not answer him; and lay my staff on the boy's face."
verses.4:30: But the boy's mother said, "As the LORD lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you!" So he rose and went after her.
verses.4:31: Now Gehazi had gone on ahead of them and laid the staff on the boy's face, but there was no sound and no response. So he returned to meet him and told him, saying, "The boy has not awakened."
verses.4:32: When Elisha came into the house, there was the boy, dead, laid upon his bed.
verses.4:33: So he went in, shut the door behind the two of them, and prayed to the LORD.
verses.4:34: Then he climbed up and lay upon the child, and put his mouth on his mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his palms on his palms; and he bent over him, and the flesh of the child became warm.
verses.4:35: Then he turned back and walked in the house, once this way and once that way, and climbed up and bent over him. And the boy sneezed seven times, and the boy opened his eyes.
verses.4:36: Then he called to Gehazi and said, "Call this Shunammite woman." So he called her, and she came to him. And he said, "Pick up your son."
verses.4:37: She came in, fell at his feet, and bowed down to the ground; then she picked up her son and went out.
verses.4:38: Now Elisha returned to Gilgal, and there was a famine in the land. While the sons of the prophets were sitting before him, he said to his servant, "Put on the large pot and boil stew for the sons of the prophets."
verses.4:39: Then one of them went out into the field to gather herbs, and found a wild vine and gathered from it wild gourds, a garment full; and he came and sliced them into the pot of stew, because they did not know them.
verses.4:40: Then they poured it out for the men to eat. And as they were eating from the stew, they cried out and said, "There is death in the pot, man of God!" And they could not eat it.
verses.4:41: But he said, "Then bring flour." And he threw it into the pot and said, "Pour it out for the people that they may eat." And there was nothing harmful in the pot.
verses.4:42: Now a man came from Baal-shalishah and brought to the man of God bread of the firstfruits, twenty loaves of barley and fresh ears of grain in his sack. And he said, "Give it to the people that they may eat."
verses.4:43: But his attendant said, "How can I set this before a hundred men?" Yet he said, "Give it to the people that they may eat, for this is what the LORD says, 'They shall eat and have some left over.'"
verses.4:44: So he set it before them, and they ate and had some left over, according to the word of the LORD.
verses.5:1: Now Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Aram, was a great man before his master and highly esteemed, because through him the LORD had given deliverance to Aram. The man was a mighty warrior, yet he was leprous.
verses.5:2: Now the Arameans had gone out in raiding bands and had taken captive a young girl from the land of Israel, and she attended Naaman's wife.
verses.5:3: She said to her mistress, "If only my master were before the prophet who is in Samaria! Then he would cure him of his leprosy."
verses.5:4: So he went in and told his master, saying, "Thus and thus spoke the girl who is from the land of Israel."
verses.5:5: Then the king of Aram said, "Go ahead, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel." So he departed and took with him ten talents of silver, six thousand pieces of gold, and ten changes of garments.
verses.5:6: And he brought the letter to the king of Israel, saying, "Now when this letter comes to you, see, I have sent Naaman my servant to you, so that you may cure him of his leprosy."
verses.5:7: When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his garments and said, "Am I God, to put to death and to make alive, that this one sends to me to cure a man of his leprosy? Indeed, only consider now and see that he is seeking a quarrel against me!"
verses.5:8: When Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel had torn his garments, he sent word to the king, saying, "Why have you torn your garments? Please let him come to me, and he will know that there is a prophet in Israel."
verses.5:9: So Naaman came with his horses and chariot and stood at the doorway of Elisha's house.
verses.5:10: And Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, "Go and wash seven times in the Jordan, so that your flesh may be restored to you, and be clean."
verses.5:11: But Naaman became furious and walked away, and he said, "Look, I thought, 'He will surely come out to me, and stand and call on the name of the LORD his God, and wave his hand over the place and cure the leper.'
verses.5:12: Are not Amanah and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Could I not wash in them and become clean?" So he turned and went away in rage.
verses.5:13: Then his servants drew near and spoke to him and said, "My father, had the prophet spoken a great thing to you, would you not have done it? How much more, then, when he has said to you, 'Wash and be clean'?"
verses.5:14: So he went down and immersed himself in the Jordan seven times, according to the word of the man of God; and his flesh was restored like the flesh of a young boy, and he became clean.
verses.5:15: Then he returned to the man of God, he and all his company, and he came and stood before him and said, "Look now, I know that there is no God in all the earth except in Israel. And now, please take a gift from your servant."
verses.5:16: But he said, "As the LORD lives, before whom I stand, I will take nothing." And he urged him to take it, but he refused.
verses.5:17: Then Naaman said, "If not, please let a load of earth for a pair of mules be given to your servant; for your servant will no longer offer burnt offering or sacrifice to other gods, but only to the LORD.
verses.5:18: In this matter may the LORD pardon your servant: when my master goes into the house of Rimmon to bow down there, and he leans on my hand, and I bow down in the house of Rimmon—when I bow down in the house of Rimmon, may the LORD pardon your servant in this matter."
verses.5:19: And he said to him, "Go in peace." So he departed from him a short distance.
verses.5:20: Then Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, said, "Look, my master has spared this Aramean Naaman by not taking from his hand what he brought. As the LORD lives, I will surely run after him and take something from him."
verses.5:21: So Gehazi pursued after Naaman. When Naaman saw someone running after him, he stepped down from the chariot to meet him and said, "Is all well?"
verses.5:22: And he said, "All is well. My master has sent me, saying, 'Look, just now two young men from the hill country of Ephraim, from the sons of the prophets, have come to me. Please give them a talent of silver and two changes of garments.'"
verses.5:23: Naaman said, "Be pleased to take two talents." And he pressed him, and tied up two talents of silver in two bags, with two changes of garments, and handed them to two of his servants; and they carried them before him.
verses.5:24: When he came to the hill, he took them from their hand and stored them away in the house; then he sent the men away, and they departed.
verses.5:25: Then he went in and stood before his master. And Elisha said to him, "Where have you come from, Gehazi?" And he said, "Your servant has not gone anywhere at all."
verses.5:26: Then he said to him, "Did not my heart go along when the man turned back from his chariot to meet you? Is it a time to take the silver and to take garments, and olive groves and vineyards, and flocks and herds, and male servants and female servants?
verses.5:27: Therefore the leprosy of Naaman shall cling to you and to your seed forever." So he went out from his presence leprous, like snow.
verses.6:1: The sons of the prophets said to Elisha, "Look now, the place where we dwell before you is too cramped for us.
verses.6:2: Please let us go as far as the Jordan, and let every man take one beam from there, and let us make for ourselves a place there to dwell." So he said, "Go."
verses.6:3: Then one of them said, "Please consent and go with your servants." He replied, "I will go."
verses.6:4: He went with them, and they arrived at the Jordan and cut down the trees.
verses.6:5: Now as one of them was felling a beam, the iron fell into the water. He cried out and said, "Alas, my master, for it was borrowed!"
verses.6:6: The man of God asked, "Where did it fall?" He showed him the place, and he cut off a piece of wood, cast it there, and caused the iron to float.
verses.6:7: And he said, "Lift it up for yourself." So he stretched out his hand and took it.
verses.6:8: Now the king of Aram was waging war against Israel, and he took counsel with his servants, saying, "In such and such a place my encampment will be."
verses.6:9: Then the man of God sent word to the king of Israel, saying, "Be on your guard against passing this place, for the Arameans are coming down there."
verses.6:10: The king of Israel sent to the place about which the man of God had told him and warned him, so he kept on his guard there, not once and not twice.
verses.6:11: The heart of the king of Aram was greatly agitated over this matter, so he summoned his servants and said to them, "Will you not tell me which one of ours is for the king of Israel?"
verses.6:12: One of his servants said, "No, my lord the king; rather, Elisha, the prophet who is in Israel, tells the king of Israel the words that you speak in your bedroom."
verses.6:13: So he said, "Go and see where he is, so that I may send and take him." And it was told to him, "Look, he is in Dothan."
verses.6:14: He sent horses and chariots and a massive army there, and they came by night and surrounded the city.
verses.6:15: Now the attendant of the man of God got up early and went out, and look, an army with horses and chariots was encircling the city. His young servant said to him, "Alas, my master! What are we to do?"
verses.6:16: He answered, "Do not be afraid, for those with us are more numerous than those with them."
verses.6:17: Then Elisha prayed and said, "LORD, please open his eyes so that he may see." The LORD opened the young man's eyes, and he saw, and look, the mountain was filled with horses and chariots of fire encircling Elisha.
verses.6:18: When they came down to him, Elisha prayed to the LORD and said, "Please strike this nation with blindness." So He struck them with blindness according to the word of Elisha.
verses.6:19: Then Elisha said to them, "This is not the road, and this is not the city. Follow after me, and I will lead you to the man whom you are seeking." So he led them to Samaria.
verses.6:20: When they entered Samaria, Elisha said, "LORD, open the eyes of these men so that they may see." The LORD opened their eyes, and they saw, and look, they were in the middle of Samaria.
verses.6:21: When the king of Israel saw them, he said to Elisha, "Should I strike them down? Should I strike them down, my father?"
verses.6:22: He replied, "Do not strike them down. Would you strike down those you captured with your sword and bow? Place bread and water in front of them, and let them eat and drink and go to their master."
verses.6:23: So he prepared a great banquet for them, and they ate and drank; then he sent them away, and they went to their master. And the raiding bands of Aram did not come again into the land of Israel.
verses.6:24: After this, Ben-hadad king of Aram assembled his entire army, went up, and laid siege to Samaria.
verses.6:25: There was a great famine in Samaria, and look, they besieged it until a donkey's head went for eighty pieces of silver, and a quarter of a kab of dove's droppings for five pieces of silver.
verses.6:26: While the king of Israel was passing along the wall, a woman cried out to him, "Help, my lord the king!"
verses.6:27: He replied, "If the LORD does not help you, from where could I help you? From the threshing floor or from the winepress?"
verses.6:28: Then the king asked her, "What troubles you?" She replied, "This woman said to me, 'Give your son so that we may eat him today, and we will eat my son tomorrow.'
verses.6:29: So we boiled my son and ate him. Then on the next day I said to her, 'Give your son so that we may eat him,' but she has hidden her son."
verses.6:30: When the king heard the woman's words, he tore his garments while he was passing along the wall; and the people looked, and look, sackcloth was underneath on his flesh.
verses.6:31: Then he said, "May God do so to me, and so may He add, if the head of Elisha son of Shaphat remains on him today!"
verses.6:32: Now Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him. The king had sent a man from his presence, but before the messenger reached him, Elisha said to the elders, "Do you see that this son of a murderer has sent to remove my head? Look, when the messenger arrives, shut the door and press him back with the door. Is not the sound of his master's feet behind him?"
verses.6:33: While he was still speaking with them, look, the messenger came down to him. And he said, "Look, this calamity is from the LORD; why should I keep waiting for the LORD?"
verses.7:1: Then Elisha said, "Hear the word of the LORD! This is what the LORD says: 'About this time tomorrow, a seah of fine flour will go for a shekel, and two seahs of barley for a shekel, at the gate of Samaria.'"
verses.7:2: Then the officer on whose hand the king leaned answered the man of God and said, "Look, if the LORD should make windows in the heavens, could this thing happen?" And he said, "Look, you will see it with your own eyes, yet you will not eat any of it."
verses.7:3: Now four leprous men were at the entrance of the gate, and they said to one another, "Why are we sitting here until we die?
verses.7:4: If we say, 'We will enter the city,' the famine is in the city, and we will die there; and if we sit here, we will die. So now, come, let us surrender to the camp of Aram. If they let us live, we will live; and if they put us to death, then we will die."
verses.7:5: So they rose at twilight to go to the camp of Aram; and when they came to the edge of the camp of Aram, look, no one was there.
verses.7:6: For the Lord had caused the camp of Aram to hear the sound of chariots, the sound of horses, the sound of a great army. So they said to one another, "Look, the king of Israel has hired the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Egypt against us to come upon us!"
verses.7:7: Therefore they rose and fled at twilight, and they abandoned their tents, their horses, and their donkeys, the camp just as it was, and fled for their lives.
verses.7:8: When these leprous men came to the edge of the camp, they entered one tent and ate and drank, and they carried away silver, gold, and garments from there, and went and hid them. Then they returned and entered another tent, carried things away from there, and went and hid them.
verses.7:9: Then they said to one another, "We are not doing right. This day is a day of good news, yet we are keeping silent. If we wait until the light of morning, punishment will overtake us. So now, come, let us go and report at the king's palace."
verses.7:10: So they came and called out to the gatekeepers of the city, and they told them, saying, "We went to the camp of Aram, and look, no one was there and no human voice, only the horses tied up, the donkeys tied up, and the tents just as they were."
verses.7:11: Then the gatekeepers called out, and they reported it inside the king's palace.
verses.7:12: The king rose in the night and said to his servants, "Let me tell you now what the Arameans have done to us. They know that we are hungry, so they have left the camp to hide themselves in the field, saying, 'When they come out of the city, we will capture them alive and enter the city.'"
verses.7:13: Then one of his servants answered and said, "Please let them take five of the remaining horses that are left in it—look, they are like all the multitude of Israel who are left in it; look, they are like all the multitude of Israel who have perished—and let us send and see."
verses.7:14: So they took two chariots with horses, and the king sent them after the army of Aram, saying, "Go and see."
verses.7:15: They went after them as far as the Jordan, and look, the entire road was full of garments and equipment that the Arameans had thrown away in their haste. Then the messengers returned and told the king.
verses.7:16: So the people went out and plundered the camp of Aram. Then a seah of fine flour went for a shekel, and two seahs of barley for a shekel, according to the word of the LORD.
verses.7:17: Now the king had appointed the officer on whose hand he leaned to be in charge of the gate, but the people trampled him in the gate, and he died, just as the man of God had spoken, who spoke when the king came down to him.
verses.7:18: For when the man of God had spoken to the king, saying, "Two seahs of barley will go for a shekel, and a seah of fine flour for a shekel, about this time tomorrow at the gate of Samaria,"
verses.7:19: the officer had answered the man of God and said, "Now look, if the LORD should make windows in the heavens, could anything like this happen?" And he had said, "Look, you will see it with your own eyes, yet you will not eat any of it."
verses.7:20: So it happened to him; the people trampled him in the gate, and he died.
verses.8:1: Now Elisha spoke to the woman whose son he had brought back to life, saying, "Get up and go, you and your household, and sojourn wherever you can sojourn, for the LORD has summoned a famine, and it is indeed coming upon the land for seven years."
verses.8:2: So the woman got up and acted according to the word of the man of God; she and her household went and sojourned in the land of the Philistines for seven years.
verses.8:3: At the end of seven years, the woman returned from the land of the Philistines, and she went out to cry out to the king concerning her house and concerning her field.
verses.8:4: Now the king was speaking to Gehazi, the attendant of the man of God, saying, "Please recount to me all the great things that Elisha has done."
verses.8:5: While he was recounting to the king how he had brought the dead one back to life, look, the woman whose son he had brought back to life was crying out to the king concerning her house and concerning her field. Then Gehazi said, "My lord the king, this is the woman, and this is her son whom Elisha brought back to life."
verses.8:6: When the king questioned the woman, she recounted it to him. So the king assigned an official to her, saying, "Restore all that belongs to her and all the produce of the field, from the day she left the land until now."
verses.8:7: Then Elisha came to Damascus. Now Ben-hadad king of Aram was sick, and it was reported to him, saying, "The man of God has come as far as here."
verses.8:8: The king said to Hazael, "Take a gift in your hand and go to meet the man of God, and inquire of the LORD through him, saying, 'Will I recover from this sickness?'"
verses.8:9: So Hazael went to meet him and took a gift in his hand, even every good thing of Damascus, a load of forty camels. He came and stood before him and said, "Your son Ben-hadad king of Aram has sent me to you, saying, 'Will I recover from this sickness?'"
verses.8:10: Elisha said to him, "Go, say to him, 'You will surely recover,' yet the LORD has shown me that he will surely die."
verses.8:11: He fixed his gaze and kept it set to the point of embarrassment, and the man of God wept.
verses.8:12: Hazael said, "Why is my lord weeping?" And he said, "Because I know the evil that you will do to the sons of Israel: their strongholds you will set on fire, their young men you will kill with the sword, their little ones you will dash to pieces, and their pregnant women you will rip open."
verses.8:13: Hazael said, "But what is your servant, a dog, that he should do this great thing?" Elisha answered, "The LORD has shown me that you will be king over Aram."
verses.8:14: So he departed from Elisha and came to his master, who said to him, "What did Elisha say to you?" He answered, "He said to me, 'You will surely recover.'"
verses.8:15: On the next day, he took the bedcover, dipped it in water, and spread it over his face, and he died. Then Hazael became king in his place.
verses.8:16: Now in the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, while Jehoshaphat was king of Judah, Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, became king.
verses.8:17: He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
verses.8:18: He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done, for a daughter of Ahab was his wife; and he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
verses.8:19: Yet the LORD was not willing to destroy Judah, for the sake of His servant David, just as He had promised him to give him a lamp for his sons always.
verses.8:20: In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah and set a king over themselves.
verses.8:21: So Joram crossed over to Zair, and all the chariots were with him. He arose by night and struck down Edom, who had surrounded him, and the chariot commanders, but the troops fled to their tents.
verses.8:22: Thus Edom has been in revolt from under the hand of Judah to this day. Then Libnah revolted at that time.
verses.8:23: Now the rest of the deeds of Joram, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.8:24: So Joram lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David, and his son Ahaziah became king in his place.
verses.8:25: In the twelfth year of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, Ahaziah son of Jehoram, king of Judah, became king.
verses.8:26: Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Athaliah, daughter of Omri king of Israel.
verses.8:27: He walked in the way of the house of Ahab and did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, just like the house of Ahab, for he was related by marriage to the house of Ahab.
verses.8:28: He went with Joram son of Ahab to battle against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-Gilead, and the Arameans wounded Joram.
verses.8:29: So King Joram returned to be healed in Jezreel from the wounds that the Arameans had inflicted on him at Ramah when he fought against Hazael king of Aram. And Ahaziah son of Jehoram, king of Judah, went down to see Joram son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he was sick.
verses.9:1: Now Elisha the prophet summoned one of the sons of the prophets and said to him, "Gird your waist, take this flask of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth-Gilead.
verses.9:2: When you arrive there, look there for Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi; go in, have him rise from among his brothers, and bring him into an inner room.
verses.9:3: Then take the flask of oil and pour it on his head, and say, 'This is what the LORD says: I have anointed you as king over Israel.' Then open the door and flee, and do not wait."
verses.9:4: So the young man, the young prophet, went to Ramoth-Gilead.
verses.9:5: When he arrived, look, the commanders of the army were sitting there. He said, "I have a word for you, commander." Jehu asked, "For which one of all of us?" He replied, "For you, commander."
verses.9:6: So he rose and went into the house; then he poured the oil on his head and said to him, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'I have anointed you as king over the people of the LORD, over Israel.
verses.9:7: You shall strike down the house of Ahab your master, that I may avenge the blood of My servants the prophets and the blood of all the servants of the LORD from the hand of Jezebel.
verses.9:8: The whole house of Ahab shall perish, and I will cut off from Ahab every male, both bound and free, in Israel.
verses.9:9: And I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah.
verses.9:10: As for Jezebel, the dogs will eat her in the plot of Jezreel, and there will be no one to bury her.'" Then he opened the door and fled.
verses.9:11: When Jehu came out to his master's servants, one said to him, "Is it peace? Why did this madman come to you?" He said to them, "You yourselves know the man and his talk."
verses.9:12: They said, "That is a lie! Please tell us." So he said, "Such and such he said to me, saying, 'This is what the LORD says: I have anointed you as king over Israel.'"
verses.9:13: Then they hurried, and each man took his garment and laid it beneath him on the bare steps; and they blew the ram's horn and said, "Jehu is king!"
verses.9:14: So Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi, conspired against Joram. Now Joram had been keeping guard at Ramoth-Gilead, he and all Israel, against Hazael king of Aram.
verses.9:15: But King Jehoram had returned to be healed in Jezreel from the wounds that the Arameans had inflicted on him when he fought against Hazael king of Aram. So Jehu said, "If this is your wish, let no escapee leave the city to go and report it in Jezreel."
verses.9:16: Then Jehu mounted up and went to Jezreel, for Joram was lying there. And Ahaziah king of Judah had gone down to see Joram.
verses.9:17: Now the watchman was standing on the tower in Jezreel, and he saw the company of Jehu as he approached, and he said, "I see a company." Jehoram said, "Take a horseman and send him to meet them, and let him say, 'Is it peace?'"
verses.9:18: So the horseman went to meet him and said, "This is what the king says: 'Is it peace?'" Jehu answered, "What do you have to do with peace? Turn behind me!" Then the watchman reported, saying, "The messenger reached them, but he has not returned."
verses.9:19: So he sent a second horseman, who came to them and said, "This is what the king says: 'Peace?'" Jehu answered, "What do you have to do with peace? Turn behind me!"
verses.9:20: The watchman reported, saying, "He reached them, and he has not returned. And the driving is like the driving of Jehu son of Nimshi, for he drives madly."
verses.9:21: Jehoram said, "Hitch up!" So they hitched his chariot. Then Jehoram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah went out, each in his chariot; they went out to meet Jehu and found him at the plot of Naboth the Jezreelite.
verses.9:22: When Jehoram saw Jehu, he said, "Is it peace, Jehu?" He replied, "What peace can there be so long as there are the prostitutions of your mother Jezebel and her many sorceries?"
verses.9:23: Then Jehoram turned his hands and fled, and he said to Ahaziah, "Treachery, Ahaziah!"
verses.9:24: But Jehu filled his hand with the bow and struck Jehoram between his shoulders; the arrow came out through his heart, and he slumped down in his chariot.
verses.9:25: Then he said to Bidkar his officer, "Lift him up and throw him into the plot of the field of Naboth the Jezreelite; for remember how, when you and I were riding in pairs behind his father Ahab, the LORD laid this oracle upon him:
verses.9:26: 'Surely I saw the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons yesterday, declares the LORD, and I will repay you on this plot, declares the LORD.' Now then, lift him up and throw him into the plot, according to the word of the LORD."
verses.9:27: When Ahaziah king of Judah saw this, he fled by way of Beth-Haggan. Jehu pursued after him and said, "Strike him too in the chariot!" at the ascent of Gur, which is near Ibleam. And he fled to Megiddo and died there.
verses.9:28: His servants carried him by chariot to Jerusalem and buried him in his tomb with his fathers in the city of David.
verses.9:29: Now in the eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab, Ahaziah became king over Judah.
verses.9:30: When Jehu came to Jezreel, Jezebel heard of it; she painted her eyes with kohl, adorned her head, and looked out through the window.
verses.9:31: As Jehu entered the gate, she said, "Is it peace, Zimri, killer of his master?"
verses.9:32: He lifted his face toward the window and said, "Who is with me? Who?" And two or three eunuchs looked out at him.
verses.9:33: He said, "Throw her down!" So they threw her down, and some of her blood spattered on the wall and on the horses, and he trampled her.
verses.9:34: Then he went inside, ate, and drank, and he said, "Attend now to this cursed woman and bury her, for she is a king's daughter."
verses.9:35: So they went to bury her, but they found nothing of her except the skull, the feet, and the palms of the hands.
verses.9:36: They returned and reported it to him. And he said, "This is the word of the LORD that He spoke by the hand of His servant Elijah the Tishbite, saying, 'In the plot of Jezreel the dogs will eat the flesh of Jezebel,
verses.9:37: and the corpse of Jezebel will be like dung on the surface of the field in the plot of Jezreel, so that they will not say, "This is Jezebel."'"
verses.10:1: Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. So Jehu wrote letters and sent them to Samaria, to the officials of Jezreel, the elders, and to the guardians of Ahab, saying,
verses.10:2: "And now, as soon as this letter reaches you, since the sons of your master are with you, and with you are the chariotry and the horses, and a fortified city and the weapons,
verses.10:3: choose the best and most upright among the sons of your master, and set him on the throne of his father, and fight for the house of your master."
verses.10:4: But they feared exceedingly, and they said, "Look, the two kings did not stand before him, so how can we ourselves stand?"
verses.10:5: So the one over the household, and the one over the city, along with the elders and the guardians, sent word to Jehu, saying, "We are your servants, and all that you say to us we will do. We will not make any man king; do what is good in your eyes."
verses.10:6: Then he wrote a letter to them a second time, saying, "If you are for me and listen to my voice, take the heads of the men, the sons of your master, and come to me at Jezreel about this time tomorrow." Now the king's sons, seventy men, were with the great men of the city, who were bringing them up.
verses.10:7: And when the letter reached them, they took the sons of the king and slaughtered seventy men; then they put their heads in baskets and sent them to him at Jezreel.
verses.10:8: And the messenger arrived and reported to him, saying, "They have brought the heads of the king's sons." And he said, "Place them in two heaps at the entrance of the gate until the morning."
verses.10:9: And it happened in the morning that he went out and stood and said to all the people, "You are innocent. Look, I conspired against my master and killed him, yet who struck down all these?
verses.10:10: Know then that nothing from the word of the LORD will fall to the ground, which the LORD spoke concerning the house of Ahab; and the LORD has done what He spoke by the hand of His servant Elijah."
verses.10:11: Then Jehu struck down all who remained of the house of Ahab in Jezreel, along with all his great men, his close friends, and his priests, until he left him no survivor.
verses.10:12: Then he arose and came and went toward Samaria; he was at Beth-eked of the Shepherds along the road.
verses.10:13: And Jehu met the brothers of Ahaziah king of Judah, and he said, "Who are you?" And they said, "We are the brothers of Ahaziah, and we have come down to greet the sons of the king and the sons of the queen mother."
verses.10:14: And he said, "Seize them alive!" So they seized them alive and slaughtered them at the cistern of Beth-eked, forty-two men; and he did not leave a single man of them.
verses.10:15: And he went from there and met Jehonadab son of Rechab coming toward him, and he greeted him and said to him, "Is your heart upright, just as my heart is with your heart?" And Jehonadab said, "It is, indeed it is!" "Give me your hand." So he gave his hand, and he brought him up to himself into the chariot.
verses.10:16: And he said, "Come with me and look upon my zeal for the LORD." So they had him ride in his chariot.
verses.10:17: When he came to Samaria, he struck down all who remained of Ahab in Samaria until he destroyed them, according to the word of the LORD which He spoke to Elijah.
verses.10:18: Then Jehu assembled all the people and said to them, "Ahab served Baal a little; Jehu will serve him greatly.
verses.10:19: So now summon to me all the prophets of Baal, all his worshipers, and all his priests; let not a man be missing, for I have a great sacrifice for Baal. Everyone who is missing will not live." But Jehu acted with cunning in order to destroy the worshipers of Baal.
verses.10:20: And Jehu said, "Consecrate a solemn assembly for Baal." So they proclaimed it.
verses.10:21: Then Jehu sent word through all Israel, and all the worshipers of Baal arrived, so that not a single man was left who did not come. They entered the house of Baal, and the house of Baal was filled from end to end.
verses.10:22: And he said to the one over the wardrobe, "Bring out robes for all the worshipers of Baal." So he brought out the robes for them.
verses.10:23: Then Jehu and Jehonadab son of Rechab entered the house of Baal, and he said to the worshipers of Baal, "Search and see that there are none of the servants of the LORD here with you, but only the worshipers of Baal alone."
verses.10:24: Then they went in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Now Jehu had stationed eighty men for himself outside and had said, "Whoever lets anyone escape from the men I am bringing into your hands, his life will be in place of that man's life."
verses.10:25: And it happened, as soon as he finished offering the burnt offering, that Jehu said to the guards and to the officers, "Go in and strike them down; let not a man come out!" So they struck them down with the edge of the sword; and the guards and the officers threw them out and went as far as the citadel of the house of Baal.
verses.10:26: Then they brought out the standing pillars of the house of Baal and burned them.
verses.10:27: And they tore down the standing pillar of Baal, and they tore down the house of Baal and turned it into a latrine to this day.
verses.10:28: So Jehu destroyed Baal from Israel.
verses.10:29: Yet as for the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, by which he made Israel sin, Jehu did not turn aside from following them—the golden calves that were at Bethel and at Dan.
verses.10:30: And the LORD said to Jehu, "Because you have done well in doing what is right in My eyes, and have done to the house of Ahab according to everything that was in My heart, sons to the fourth generation will sit for you on the throne of Israel."
verses.10:31: Yet Jehu did not take care to walk in the law of the LORD, the God of Israel, with all his heart; he did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam, by which he made Israel sin.
verses.10:32: In those days the LORD began to cut away at Israel, and Hazael struck them down throughout all the territory of Israel:
verses.10:33: from the Jordan toward the rising of the sun, all the land of Gilead—the Gadites, the Reubenites, and the Manassites—from Aroer, which is by the valley of the Arnon, both Gilead and Bashan.
verses.10:34: Now the rest of the deeds of Jehu, and everything that he did, and all his might, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.10:35: And Jehu lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria; and Jehoahaz his son reigned in his place.
verses.10:36: Now the days that Jehu reigned over Israel were twenty-eight years in Samaria.
verses.11:1: Now Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, saw that her son was dead, and she arose and destroyed all the royal seed.
verses.11:2: But Jehosheba, daughter of King Joram and sister of Ahaziah, took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the king's sons who were being put to death—him and his nurse, into the bedroom—and they hid him from Athaliah, so that he was not put to death.
verses.11:3: And he stayed with her in the house of the LORD in hiding for six years, while Athaliah was reigning over the land.
verses.11:4: Then in the seventh year Jehoiada sent and took the commanders of hundreds of the Carites and of the guards, and brought them to himself into the house of the LORD. He made a covenant with them and put them under oath in the house of the LORD, and he showed them the king's son.
verses.11:5: And he commanded them, saying, "This is the thing that you are to do: one third of you who come in on the Sabbath shall keep the watch of the king's house;
verses.11:6: and one third shall be at the gate of Sur, and one third at the gate behind the guards; so you shall keep the watch of the house as a barrier.
verses.11:7: And the two divisions among you, all who go out on the Sabbath, shall keep the watch of the house of the LORD for the king.
verses.11:8: And you shall surround the king on every side, each man with his weapons in his hand; and whoever enters the ranks shall be put to death. And be with the king when he goes out and when he comes in."
verses.11:9: So the commanders of hundreds did according to everything that Jehoiada the priest had commanded. Each man took his men—those coming in on the Sabbath together with those going out on the Sabbath—and they came to Jehoiada the priest.
verses.11:10: And the priest gave to the commanders of hundreds the spears and the shields that had belonged to King David, which were in the house of the LORD.
verses.11:11: Then the guards stood, every man with his weapons in his hand, from the right side of the house as far as the left side of the house, alongside the altar and the house, on every side around the king.
verses.11:12: Then he brought out the king's son and placed upon him the crown and the testimony; and they made him king and anointed him, and they clapped their hands and said, "May the king live!"
verses.11:13: When Athaliah heard the sound of the guards and the people, she came to the people at the house of the LORD.
verses.11:14: She looked, and there was the king standing by the pillar according to the custom, with the commanders and the trumpeters beside the king, and all the people of the land rejoicing and blowing trumpets. Then Athaliah tore her garments and cried out, "Treason! Treason!"
verses.11:15: Then Jehoiada the priest commanded the commanders of hundreds who were appointed over the army and said to them, "Bring her out between the ranks, and whoever follows her, put to death with the sword." For the priest had said, "Let her not be put to death in the house of the LORD."
verses.11:16: So they laid hands on her, and she went by way of the horses' entrance to the king's house, and there she was put to death.
verses.11:17: Then Jehoiada made the covenant between the LORD and the king and the people, that they would be a people for the LORD, and also between the king and the people.
verses.11:18: And all the people of the land went to the house of Baal and tore it down; its altars and its images they thoroughly shattered, and they killed Mattan, the priest of Baal, before the altars. And the priest set overseers over the house of the LORD.
verses.11:19: Then he took the commanders of hundreds, the Carites, the guards, and all the people of the land, and they brought the king down from the house of the LORD and came by way of the gate of the guards to the king's house. And he sat on the throne of the kings.
verses.11:20: So all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet; for they had put Athaliah to death with the sword at the king's house.
verses.12:1: Jehoash was seven years of age when he became king.
verses.12:2: In the seventh year of Jehu, Jehoash began to reign, and for forty years he reigned in Jerusalem; the name of his mother was Zibiah from Beersheba.
verses.12:3: And Jehoash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD through all his days in which Jehoiada the priest taught him.
verses.12:4: Only the high places were not removed; still the people were sacrificing and burning incense at the high places.
verses.12:5: Then Jehoash said to the priests, "All the silver of the consecrated things that is brought into the house of the LORD—current silver, each man's silver of personal valuation, all the silver that arises in a man's heart to bring into the house of the LORD—
verses.12:6: let the priests take it for themselves, each man from his acquaintance; and they themselves shall repair the damage of the house, wherever any damage is found there."
verses.12:7: Yet it happened in the twenty-third year of King Jehoash that the priests had not repaired the damage of the house.
verses.12:8: So King Jehoash summoned Jehoiada the priest and the priests and said to them, "Why are you not repairing the damage of the house? Now then, do not take silver from your acquaintances, but give it for the damage of the house."
verses.12:9: So the priests consented not to take silver from the people and not to repair the damage of the house.
verses.12:10: Then Jehoiada the priest took a chest, bored a hole in its lid, and placed it beside the altar, on the right side as one enters the house of the LORD; and the priests, the keepers of the threshold, would put into it all the silver brought into the house of the LORD.
verses.12:11: Whenever they saw that there was abundant silver in the chest, the king's scribe and the high priest would go up, tie it up in bags, and count the silver found in the house of the LORD.
verses.12:12: Then they would hand over the weighed silver into the hands of those doing the work who were placed in charge of the house of the LORD, and they would pay it out to the woodworkers and to the builders working on the house of the LORD,
verses.12:13: and to the masons and the stonecutters, and to buy timber and quarried stone to repair the damage of the house of the LORD, and for everything expended on the house for repair.
verses.12:14: However, no silver basins, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, trumpets, or any vessel of gold or vessel of silver were made for the house of the LORD from the silver brought into the house of the LORD.
verses.12:15: Rather, they would give it to those doing the work, and with it they would repair the house of the LORD.
verses.12:16: And they did not demand an accounting from the men into whose hand they gave the silver to hand over to those doing the work, for they acted with faithfulness.
verses.12:17: Silver from a guilt offering and silver from sin offerings was not brought into the house of the LORD; they belonged to the priests.
verses.12:18: At that time Hazael king of Aram went up, fought against Gath, and captured it; then Hazael set his face to go up against Jerusalem.
verses.12:19: So Jehoash king of Judah took all the consecrated things that Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah, his fathers, the kings of Judah, had consecrated, and his own consecrated things, and all the gold found in the treasuries of the house of the LORD and the house of the king, and sent them to Hazael king of Aram; and he withdrew from Jerusalem.
verses.12:20: Now the rest of the deeds of Joash and everything he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.12:21: His servants rose up, formed a conspiracy, and struck down Joash at Beth-millo, which goes down to Silla.
verses.12:22: Jozacar son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer, his servants, struck him down, and he died. They buried him with his fathers in the city of David, and his son Amaziah reigned in his place.
verses.13:1: In the twenty-third year of Joash son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king over Israel in Samaria, reigning seventeen years.
verses.13:2: And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and walked after the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, by which he caused Israel to sin; he did not turn aside from them.
verses.13:3: So the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He delivered them into the hand of Hazael king of Aram and into the hand of Ben-hadad son of Hazael all those days.
verses.13:4: Then Jehoahaz implored the favor of the LORD, and the LORD listened to him, because He saw the oppression of Israel, that the king of Aram had oppressed them.
verses.13:5: So the LORD gave Israel a deliverer, and they came out from under the hand of Aram; and the sons of Israel lived in their tents as before.
verses.13:6: Yet they did not turn aside from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, by which he caused Israel to sin; he walked in them, and the Asherah also remained standing in Samaria.
verses.13:7: For no troops had been left to Jehoahaz except fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand foot soldiers, because the king of Aram had destroyed them and made them like dust in threshing.
verses.13:8: Now the rest of the deeds of Jehoahaz and everything he did, and his might, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.13:9: So Jehoahaz lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria; and his son Joash became king in his place.
verses.13:10: In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz became king over Israel in Samaria, reigning sixteen years.
verses.13:11: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD; he did not turn aside from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, by which he caused Israel to sin, but walked in them.
verses.13:12: Now the rest of the deeds of Joash and everything he did, and his might with which he fought against Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.13:13: And Joash lay down with his fathers, and Jeroboam sat upon his throne; and Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.
verses.13:14: Now Elisha had fallen ill with his illness from which he would die; and Joash king of Israel went down to him, wept over his face, and said, "My father, my father! The chariot of Israel and its horsemen!"
verses.13:15: And Elisha said to him, "Take a bow and arrows." So he took for himself a bow and arrows.
verses.13:16: Then he said to the king of Israel, "Set your hand on the bow." And he set his hand on it, and Elisha placed his hands upon the hands of the king.
verses.13:17: He said, "Open the window eastward," and he opened it. Then Elisha said, "Shoot!" And he shot. And he said, "The LORD's arrow of deliverance, and an arrow of deliverance over Aram! You will strike Aram at Aphek until you bring them to an end."
verses.13:18: Then he said, "Take the arrows," and he took them. He said to the king of Israel, "Strike the ground!" So he struck three times and halted.
verses.13:19: Then the man of God grew angry with him and said, "You ought to have struck five or six times; then you would have struck Aram until you had brought them to an end, but now you will strike Aram three times."
verses.13:20: Then Elisha died, and they buried him. Now raiding bands of Moab would come into the land at the coming of the year.
verses.13:21: It happened, while they were burying a man, that suddenly they saw the raiding band, so they threw the man into Elisha's tomb; and the man went in and touched the bones of Elisha, and he came to life and rose up on his feet.
verses.13:22: Now Hazael king of Aram had oppressed Israel through all the days of Jehoahaz.
verses.13:23: Yet the LORD showed them grace, had compassion on them, and turned toward them for the sake of His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; He was not willing to destroy them, nor did He cast them away from His presence until now.
verses.13:24: Then Hazael king of Aram died, and his son Ben-hadad reigned in his place.
verses.13:25: Then Jehoash son of Jehoahaz took back the cities from the hand of Ben-hadad son of Hazael, which he had taken from the hand of his father Jehoahaz in war. Three times Joash defeated him and restored the cities of Israel.
verses.14:1: In the second year of Joash son of Joahaz, king of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, began to reign.
verses.14:2: He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jehoaddan from Jerusalem.
verses.14:3: He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, though not like his father David; he did according to everything his father Joash had done.
verses.14:4: Only the high places were not removed; the people were still sacrificing and burning incense on the high places.
verses.14:5: Now when the kingdom grew strong in his hand, he struck down his servants who had struck down his father the king.
verses.14:6: Yet he did not put to death the sons of those who had struck him down, in accordance with what is written in the book of the law of Moses, in which the LORD commanded, saying, "Fathers shall not be put to death on account of sons, and sons shall not be put to death on account of fathers; instead, each man shall be put to death for his own sin."
verses.14:7: He struck down ten thousand of Edom in the Valley of Salt, captured Sela in battle, and called its name Joktheel, to this day.
verses.14:8: Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, "Come, let us look each other in the face."
verses.14:9: Then Jehoash king of Israel sent word to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, "The thornbush that was in Lebanon sent word to the cedar that was in Lebanon, saying, 'Give your daughter to my son for a wife.' Then a wild animal of the field that was in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thornbush.
verses.14:10: You have indeed struck down Edom, and your heart has lifted you up. Relish your honor and remain in your house; for why should you stir up disaster so that you fall, you and Judah with you?"
verses.14:11: Amaziah, however, did not listen. So Jehoash king of Israel went up, and they looked each other in the face, he and Amaziah king of Judah, at Beth-shemesh, which belongs to Judah.
verses.14:12: And Judah was routed before Israel, and they fled, each man to his tent.
verses.14:13: Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, son of Jehoash, son of Ahaziah, at Beth-shemesh. Then he came to Jerusalem and breached the wall of Jerusalem from the Gate of Ephraim to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.
verses.14:14: He took all the gold and silver and all the vessels that were found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the king's house, as well as the hostages, and returned to Samaria.
verses.14:15: As for the rest of the deeds of Jehoash that he did, and his might, and how he fought with Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.14:16: Then Jehoash lay down with his fathers and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel, and his son Jeroboam reigned in his place.
verses.14:17: Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, lived fifteen years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel.
verses.14:18: As for the rest of the deeds of Amaziah, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.14:19: They formed a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish; yet they sent after him to Lachish and put him to death there.
verses.14:20: Then they carried him on horses, and he was buried in Jerusalem with his fathers in the City of David.
verses.14:21: Then all the people of Judah took Azariah, when he was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
verses.14:22: He built Elath and restored it to Judah after the king lay down with his fathers.
verses.14:23: In the fifteenth year of Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel, became king in Samaria for forty-one years.
verses.14:24: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD; he did not turn aside from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, with which he caused Israel to sin.
verses.14:25: He restored the border of Israel from Lebo-hamath to the Sea of the Arabah, in accordance with the word of the LORD, the God of Israel, which He spoke by the hand of His servant Jonah son of Amittai, the prophet who was from Gath-hepher.
verses.14:26: For the LORD saw that the affliction of Israel was very bitter; there was no one bond and no one free, and there was no helper for Israel.
verses.14:27: Yet the LORD had not spoken of blotting out the name of Israel from under heaven, so He saved them by the hand of Jeroboam son of Joash.
verses.14:28: As for the rest of the deeds of Jeroboam and all that he did, and his might, how he fought, and how he restored Damascus and Hamath for Judah in Israel, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.14:29: Then Jeroboam lay down with his fathers, with the kings of Israel, and his son Zechariah reigned in his place.
verses.15:1: In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah, king of Judah, began to reign.
verses.15:2: He was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jecoliah from Jerusalem.
verses.15:3: He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, according to everything his father Amaziah had done.
verses.15:4: Only the high places were not removed; the people were still sacrificing and burning incense on the high places.
verses.15:5: And the LORD afflicted the king so that he was a leper until the day of his death, and he lived in a separate house; meanwhile, Jotham the king's son was over the household, judging the people of the land.
verses.15:6: As for the rest of the deeds of Azariah and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.15:7: Then Azariah lay down with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the City of David, and his son Jotham reigned in his place.
verses.15:8: In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah, Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in Samaria for six months.
verses.15:9: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as his fathers had done; he did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, with which he caused Israel to sin.
verses.15:10: Then Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against him, struck him down in front of the people, put him to death, and reigned in his place.
verses.15:11: As for the rest of the deeds of Zechariah, see, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
verses.15:12: This was the word of the LORD that He spoke to Jehu, saying, "Sons of yours to the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel." And so it was.
verses.15:13: Shallum son of Jabesh began to reign in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah, and he reigned a full month in Samaria.
verses.15:14: Then Menahem son of Gadi went up from Tirzah and came to Samaria, and he struck down Shallum son of Jabesh in Samaria, put him to death, and reigned in his place.
verses.15:15: As for the rest of the deeds of Shallum and his conspiracy that he formed, see, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
verses.15:16: At that time Menahem struck down Tiphsah and all who were in it and its territory from Tirzah, because it did not open; so he struck it down and ripped open all its pregnant women.
verses.15:17: In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Menahem son of Gadi became king over Israel for ten years in Samaria.
verses.15:18: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD; he did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, with which he caused Israel to sin, all his days.
verses.15:19: Pul king of Assyria came against the land, and Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver so that his hands might be with him to strengthen the kingdom in his hand.
verses.15:20: Menahem exacted the silver from Israel, from all the men of wealth, to give to the king of Assyria, fifty shekels of silver per man. Then the king of Assyria turned back and did not stay there in the land.
verses.15:21: As for the rest of the deeds of Menahem and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.15:22: Then Menahem lay down with his fathers, and his son Pekahiah reigned in his place.
verses.15:23: In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekahiah son of Menahem became king over Israel in Samaria for two years.
verses.15:24: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD; he did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, with which he caused Israel to sin.
verses.15:25: Then Pekah son of Remaliah, his officer, conspired against him and struck him down in Samaria, in the citadel of the king's house, with Argob and Arieh, and with him were fifty men from the sons of the Gileadites; and he put him to death and reigned in his place.
verses.15:26: As for the rest of the deeds of Pekahiah and all that he did, see, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
verses.15:27: In the fifty-second year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekah son of Remaliah became king over Israel in Samaria for twenty years.
verses.15:28: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD; he did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, with which he caused Israel to sin.
verses.15:29: In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria came and took Ijon, Abel-beth-maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali, and he exiled them to Assyria.
verses.15:30: Then Hoshea son of Elah formed a conspiracy against Pekah son of Remaliah, struck him down, put him to death, and reigned in his place in the twentieth year of Jotham son of Uzziah.
verses.15:31: As for the rest of the deeds of Pekah and all that he did, see, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
verses.15:32: In the second year of Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, Jotham son of Uzziah, king of Judah, began to reign.
verses.15:33: He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jerusha daughter of Zadok.
verses.15:34: He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD; he did according to everything his father Uzziah had done.
verses.15:35: Only the high places were not removed; the people were still sacrificing and burning incense on the high places. He built the upper gate of the house of the LORD.
verses.15:36: As for the rest of the deeds of Jotham that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.15:37: In those days the LORD began to send against Judah Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah.
verses.15:38: Then Jotham lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the City of David his father, and his son Ahaz reigned in his place.
verses.16:1: In the seventeenth year of Pekah son of Remaliah, Ahaz son of Jotham, king of Judah, began his reign.
verses.16:2: Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem; he did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD his God, like David his father.
verses.16:3: Instead, he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, and he even caused his son to pass through the fire, following the abominations of the nations whom the LORD had dispossessed from before the sons of Israel.
verses.16:4: He sacrificed and burned incense at the high places, on the hills, and under every lush tree.
verses.16:5: Then Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, came up to Jerusalem for battle. They laid siege to Ahaz, yet they were not able to do battle.
verses.16:6: At that time Rezin king of Aram restored Elath to Aram and cleared the Judeans out of Eloth; and Edomites came to Elath and have lived there to this day.
verses.16:7: Then Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, saying, "I am your servant and your son. Come up and save me from the grasp of the king of Aram and from the grasp of the king of Israel, who are rising up against me."
verses.16:8: Ahaz took the silver and the gold found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the king's house, and he sent a bribe to the king of Assyria.
verses.16:9: So the king of Assyria listened to him; the king of Assyria went up against Damascus, seized it, carried it into exile to Kir, and put Rezin to death.
verses.16:10: Then King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, and he saw the altar that was in Damascus. King Ahaz sent to Uriah the priest the likeness of the altar and its design, for all its workmanship.
verses.16:11: So Uriah the priest built the altar; according to everything King Ahaz had sent from Damascus, thus Uriah the priest did before King Ahaz came from Damascus.
verses.16:12: When the king came from Damascus, the king saw the altar; then the king approached the altar and went up onto it.
verses.16:13: He offered up in smoke his burnt offering and his grain offering, poured out his drink offering, and dashed the blood of the peace offerings that were his upon the altar.
verses.16:14: As for the bronze altar that was before the LORD, he moved it from the front of the house, from between the altar and the house of the LORD, and placed it on the north side of the altar.
verses.16:15: Then King Ahaz commanded Uriah the priest, saying, "On the great altar offer up in smoke the morning burnt offering and the evening grain offering, the king's burnt offering and his grain offering, and the burnt offering of all the people of the land, and their grain offering and their drink offerings; and on it you are to dash all the blood of a burnt offering and all the blood of a sacrifice. But the bronze altar will be mine for inquiry."
verses.16:16: So Uriah the priest did in accordance with all that King Ahaz had commanded.
verses.16:17: King Ahaz cut off the side panels of the stands and removed the basin from them; he also took down the sea from the bronze oxen that were under it and set it on a stone pavement.
verses.16:18: And the covered structure of the Sabbath that they had built in the house, and the king's outer entrance, he shifted at the house of the LORD because of the king of Assyria.
verses.16:19: As for the rest of the deeds of Ahaz that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.16:20: Then Ahaz lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David; and his son Hezekiah became king in his place.
verses.17:1: In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea son of Elah became king in Samaria over Israel for nine years.
verses.17:2: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, yet not like the kings of Israel who were before him.
verses.17:3: Against him Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up, and Hoshea became a servant to him and rendered tribute to him.
