verses.17:4: But the king of Assyria discovered a conspiracy in Hoshea, for he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt and had not brought up tribute to the king of Assyria as he had year by year; so the king of Assyria confined him and bound him in prison.
verses.17:5: Then the king of Assyria went up through all the land; he went up to Samaria and laid siege to it for three years.
verses.17:6: In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of Assyria captured Samaria and carried Israel into exile to Assyria; he settled them in Halah, and along the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.
verses.17:7: Now this happened because the sons of Israel had sinned against the LORD their God, who had brought them up out of the land of Egypt from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and they feared other gods.
verses.17:8: They walked in the statutes of the nations whom the LORD had dispossessed from before the sons of Israel, and in those that the kings of Israel had made.
verses.17:9: The sons of Israel did in secret things that were not right against the LORD their God; they built for themselves high places in all their cities, from watchmen's tower to fortified city.
verses.17:10: They erected for themselves standing pillars and Asherim on every high hill and under every lush tree.
verses.17:11: There they burned incense at all the high places, like the nations whom the LORD had exiled from before them, and they did evil things to provoke the LORD to anger.
verses.17:12: They served idols, about which the LORD had said to them, "You must not do this thing."
verses.17:13: Yet the LORD warned Israel and Judah by the hand of all the prophets, every seer, saying, "Turn back from your evil ways and keep My commandments, My statutes, in accordance with all the law that I commanded your fathers and that I sent to you by the hand of My servants the prophets."
verses.17:14: Yet they did not listen; instead, they stiffened their neck like the neck of their fathers, who did not trust in the LORD their God.
verses.17:15: They rejected His statutes and His covenant that He had made with their fathers, as well as His warnings with which He had warned them. They went after futility and became futile, and after the nations that were around them, concerning whom the LORD had commanded them not to act like them.
verses.17:16: They abandoned all the commandments of the LORD their God and made for themselves cast images, two calves; they made an Asherah, bowed down to all the host of heaven, and served Baal.
verses.17:17: They caused their sons and their daughters to pass through the fire, practiced divinations and read omens, and sold themselves to do what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, to provoke Him to anger.
verses.17:18: So the LORD became very angry with Israel and removed them from His presence; none remained except the tribe of Judah alone.
verses.17:19: Judah also did not keep the commandments of the LORD their God, but walked in the statutes of Israel that they had made.
verses.17:20: So the LORD rejected all the seed of Israel, afflicted them, and gave them into the hand of plunderers, until He had cast them from His presence.
verses.17:21: When He had torn Israel from the house of David, and they had made Jeroboam son of Nebat king, Jeroboam drove Israel away from following the LORD and made them sin a great sin.
verses.17:22: The sons of Israel walked in all the sins of Jeroboam that he committed; they did not turn aside from them,
verses.17:23: until the LORD removed Israel from His presence, just as He had spoken by the hand of all His servants the prophets. So Israel went into exile from its own land to Assyria to this day.
verses.17:24: Then the king of Assyria brought people from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim, and settled them in the cities of Samaria in place of the sons of Israel. They took possession of Samaria and lived in its cities.
verses.17:25: And it happened at the beginning of their living there that they did not fear the LORD; so the LORD sent lions among them, and they kept killing some of them.
verses.17:26: So they spoke to the king of Assyria, saying, "The nations that you exiled and settled in the cities of Samaria do not know the ordinance of the god of the land; so he has sent lions among them, and look, they are putting them to death, because they do not know the ordinance of the god of the land."
verses.17:27: Then the king of Assyria gave a command, saying, "Take there one of the priests whom you exiled from there, and let them go and live there, and let him teach them the ordinance of the god of the land."
verses.17:28: So one of the priests whom they had exiled from Samaria came and lived in Bethel, and he kept teaching them how they should fear the LORD.
verses.17:29: Yet each nation kept making its own gods and placed them in the houses of the high places that the Samaritans had made, each nation in their cities where they were living.
verses.17:30: The men of Babylon made Succoth-benoth, the men of Cuth made Nergal, and the men of Hamath made Ashima.
verses.17:31: The Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak, and the Sepharvites were burning their children in the fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim.
verses.17:32: They also feared the LORD, and they appointed for themselves from all their ranks priests of the high places, who officiated for them in the houses of the high places.
verses.17:33: They feared the LORD, yet they served their own gods according to the custom of the nations from which they had been carried into exile.
verses.17:34: To this day they act according to the former customs: they do not fear the LORD, nor do they act according to their statutes or their ordinance, or according to the law and the commandment that the LORD commanded the sons of Jacob, whom He named Israel.
verses.17:35: The LORD made a covenant with them and commanded them, saying, "You must not fear other gods, nor bow down to them, nor serve them, nor sacrifice to them.
verses.17:36: Rather, the LORD, who brought you up from the land of Egypt with great power and an outstretched arm, Him you must fear, and to Him you must bow down, and to Him you must sacrifice.
verses.17:37: And the statutes and the ordinances and the law and the commandment that He wrote for you, you must be careful to do all the days, and you must not fear other gods.
verses.17:38: And the covenant that I made with you, you must not forget, and you must not fear other gods.
verses.17:39: Rather, the LORD your God you must fear, and He will deliver you from the hand of all your enemies."
verses.17:40: Yet they did not listen, but they kept acting according to their former custom.
verses.17:41: So these nations feared the LORD, yet they also served their carved images; their children and their children's children also do just as their fathers did, to this day.
verses.18:1: Now it happened in the third year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, that Hezekiah son of Ahaz, king of Judah, became king.
verses.18:2: He was twenty-five years of age when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem twenty-nine years; and the name of his mother was Abi, daughter of Zechariah.
verses.18:3: And he did what was upright in the eyes of the LORD, according to everything that his father David had done.
verses.18:4: It was he who removed the high places, shattered the sacred pillars, cut down the Asherah, and crushed to pieces the bronze serpent that Moses had made; for until those days the sons of Israel had been burning incense to it, and he called it Nehushtan.
verses.18:5: In the LORD, the God of Israel, he trusted; and after him there was no one like him among all the kings of Judah, nor among those who were before him.
verses.18:6: And he clung to the LORD; he did not turn aside from following Him, and he kept His commandments that the LORD commanded Moses.
verses.18:7: The LORD was with him; wherever he went out, he met with success. And he rebelled against the king of Assyria and did not serve him.
verses.18:8: He himself struck the Philistines as far as Gaza and its borders, from watchmen's tower to fortified city.
verses.18:9: And it happened in the fourth year of King Hezekiah—that is, the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel—that Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, went up against Samaria and laid siege to it.
verses.18:10: And they captured it at the end of three years; in the sixth year of Hezekiah—that is, the ninth year of Hoshea, king of Israel—Samaria was captured.
verses.18:11: Then the king of Assyria exiled Israel to Assyria and placed them in Halah, and at the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes,
verses.18:12: because they did not listen to the voice of the LORD their God, and they transgressed His covenant—all that Moses, the servant of the LORD, had commanded—they did not listen, and they did not do it.
verses.18:13: And in the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib, king of Assyria, went up against all the fortified cities of Judah and seized them.
verses.18:14: And Hezekiah, king of Judah, sent to the king of Assyria at Lachish, saying, "I have sinned; turn back from me. Whatever you place upon me, I will bear." So the king of Assyria laid upon Hezekiah, king of Judah, three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
verses.18:15: So Hezekiah gave all the silver that was found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the house of the king.
verses.18:16: At that time Hezekiah cut off the doors of the temple of the LORD and the doorposts that Hezekiah, king of Judah, had overlaid, and gave them to the king of Assyria.
verses.18:17: Then the king of Assyria sent Tartan, Rab-saris, and Rabshakeh from Lachish to King Hezekiah with a large army to Jerusalem. And they went up and came to Jerusalem; and when they had gone up and arrived, they stood by the conduit of the upper pool, which is on the highway of the launderer's field.
verses.18:18: And they called for the king, and there went out to them Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder.
verses.18:19: And Rabshakeh said to them, "Please say to Hezekiah, 'This is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: What is this confidence in which you have trusted?
verses.18:20: You say—only talk of the lips—that there is counsel and might for the war. Now on whom have you trusted, that you rebelled against me?
verses.18:21: Now look, you have trusted in the staff of this crushed reed, in Egypt; if a man leans on it, it will go into his palm and pierce it. So is Pharaoh, king of Egypt, to all who trust in him.'
verses.18:22: And if you say to me, 'In the LORD our God we have trusted,' is He not the one whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah removed, and said to Judah and to Jerusalem, 'Before this altar you must bow down in Jerusalem'?
verses.18:23: And now, please make a wager with my master, the king of Assyria, and I will give you two thousand horses, if you are able to put riders on them yourself.
verses.18:24: And how will you turn back the face of a single governor among the least of my master's servants, while you trust in Egypt for chariots and for horsemen?
verses.18:25: Now have I come up apart from the LORD against this place to destroy it? It was the LORD who said to me, 'Go up against this land and destroy it.'"
verses.18:26: Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, Shebna, and Joah said to Rabshakeh, "Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it; and do not speak with us in Judean in the ears of the people who are on the wall."
verses.18:27: But Rabshakeh said to them, "Is it to your master and to you that my master has sent me to speak these words? Is it not to the men sitting on the wall, who are to eat their excrement and to drink the water of their feet with you?"
verses.18:28: Then Rabshakeh stood and called out in a loud voice in Judean, and spoke and said, "Hear the word of the great king, the king of Assyria.
verses.18:29: This is what the king says: Do not allow Hezekiah to deceive you, for he is not able to deliver you from his hand.
verses.18:30: And do not allow Hezekiah to cause you to trust in the LORD, saying, 'The LORD will certainly deliver us, and this city will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.'
verses.18:31: Do not listen to Hezekiah; for this is what the king of Assyria says: Make peace with me and come out to me, and eat, each one from his vine and each one from his fig tree, and drink, each one the water of his cistern,
verses.18:32: until I come and take you to a land like your land—a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of fresh olive oil and honey—so that you may live and not die. And do not listen to Hezekiah when he entices you, saying, 'The LORD will deliver us.'
verses.18:33: Have the gods of the nations actually delivered, each one his land, from the hand of the king of Assyria?
verses.18:34: Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Did they indeed deliver Samaria from my hand?
verses.18:35: Who among all the gods of the lands are those who delivered their land from my hand, so that the LORD would deliver Jerusalem from my hand?"
verses.18:36: But the people kept silent and did not answer him a word, for the command of the king was, "You must not answer him."
verses.18:37: Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Hezekiah with torn garments and reported to him the words of Rabshakeh.
verses.19:1: Now when King Hezekiah heard it, he tore his garments, covered himself in sackcloth, and went into the house of the LORD.
verses.19:2: He sent Eliakim, who was over the household, Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered in sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz.
verses.19:3: They said to him, "This is what Hezekiah says: 'This day is a day of distress, rebuke, and contempt, for children have come to the opening of the womb, and there is no strength to give birth.
verses.19:4: Perhaps the LORD your God will hear all the words of Rabshakeh, whom the king of Assyria, his master, sent to taunt the living God, and will rebuke the words that the LORD your God has heard. So lift up a prayer on behalf of the remnant that remains.'"
verses.19:5: Then the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
verses.19:6: Isaiah said to them, "This is what you shall say to your master: 'This is what the LORD says: Do not be afraid on account of the words you have heard, with which the attendants of the king of Assyria have reviled Me.
verses.19:7: Look, I am putting a spirit in him, so that he will hear a report and return to his own land, and I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.'"
verses.19:8: Then Rabshakeh turned back and found the king of Assyria waging war against Libnah, for he had heard that the king had broken camp from Lachish.
verses.19:9: When he heard concerning Tirhakah king of Cush, "Look, he has marched out to fight with you," he again sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,
verses.19:10: "Thus you shall speak to Hezekiah king of Judah, saying, 'Do not let your God in whom you trust deceive you by saying, "Jerusalem will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria."
verses.19:11: Look, you yourself have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, devoting them to destruction. And shall you be delivered?
verses.19:12: Did the gods of the nations that my fathers destroyed deliver them—Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the sons of Eden who were in Telassar?
verses.19:13: Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and of Ivvah?'"
verses.19:14: Hezekiah took the letters from the hand of the messengers and read them; then he went up to the house of the LORD, and Hezekiah spread it out before the LORD.
verses.19:15: And Hezekiah prayed before the LORD and said, "LORD, God of Israel, enthroned upon the cherubim, You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth; You made the heavens and the earth.
verses.19:16: Incline Your ear, LORD, and hear; open Your eyes, LORD, and see. Hear the words of Sennacherib that he has sent to taunt the living God.
verses.19:17: Truly, LORD, the kings of Assyria have laid waste the nations and their land,
verses.19:18: and have cast their gods into the fire; for they were not gods, only the work of human hands, wood and stone, and so they destroyed them.
verses.19:19: Now therefore, LORD our God, please save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You, LORD, are God alone."
verses.19:20: Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent word to Hezekiah, saying, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'I have heard what you prayed to Me concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria.'
verses.19:21: This is the word that the LORD has spoken concerning him: 'She has despised you, she has mocked you, the virgin daughter of Zion; she has shaken her head behind you, the daughter of Jerusalem.
verses.19:22: Whom have you taunted and reviled? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes on high? Against the Holy One of Israel!
verses.19:23: Through your messengers you have taunted the Lord, and you have said, "With my multitude of chariots I have gone up to the height of the mountains, to the farthest recesses of Lebanon; I will cut down its tallest cedars and the choicest of its cypresses, and I will enter its remotest lodging place, its lush forest.
verses.19:24: I dug and drank foreign waters, and with the sole of my feet I will dry up all the streams of Egypt."
verses.19:25: Have you not heard? Long ago I made it; from days of old I formed it. Now I have brought it to pass, that you should reduce fortified cities to desolate heaps of ruins,
verses.19:26: while their inhabitants, short of strength, were shattered and put to shame; they became plants of the field and green shoots of grass, grass on the rooftops, blighted before it reaches standing grain.
verses.19:27: Your sitting down, your going out, and your coming in I know, as well as your raging against Me.
verses.19:28: Because of your raging against Me, and because your insolence has risen to My ears, I will place My hook in your nose and My bit between your lips, and I will turn you back along the road by which you came.
verses.19:29: And this shall be the sign for you: eat self-sown growth this year, and in the second year what sprouts from that; then in the third year, sow and harvest, plant vineyards, and eat their fruit.
verses.19:30: And the escaped survivors of the house of Judah who remain shall again strike root downward and yield fruit upward.
verses.19:31: For from Jerusalem a remnant will go out, and survivors from Mount Zion. The zeal of the LORD of hosts will accomplish this.'
verses.19:32: Therefore this is what the LORD says concerning the king of Assyria: 'He will not enter this city or shoot an arrow there; he will not confront it with a shield or pile up a siege ramp against it.
verses.19:33: By the road on which he came, he will return; and this city he will not enter, declares the LORD.
verses.19:34: And I will shield this city to save it, for My own sake and for the sake of My servant David.'"
verses.19:35: That night the angel of the LORD went out and struck down one hundred eighty-five thousand in the camp of Assyria. When people rose early in the morning, look, all of them were dead bodies.
verses.19:36: Then Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp, departed, and returned, and he lived in Nineveh.
verses.19:37: And it happened, as he was bowing down in the house of Nisroch his god, that Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons struck him down with the sword, and they escaped to the land of Ararat. Then Esarhaddon his son became king in his place.
verses.20:1: In those days Hezekiah fell sick to the point of death. Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet came to him and said to him, "This is what the LORD says: 'Give instructions for your household, for you are about to die and will not live.'"
verses.20:2: Then he turned his face toward the wall and prayed to the LORD, saying,
verses.20:3: "Please, LORD, remember how I have walked before You in truth and with a whole heart, and have done what is good in Your eyes." And Hezekiah wept with great weeping.
verses.20:4: Before Isaiah had left the middle courtyard, the word of the LORD came to him, saying,
verses.20:5: "Turn back and say to Hezekiah, ruler of My people, 'This is what the LORD, the God of your father David, says: I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. Look, I am going to heal you; on the third day you shall go up to the house of the LORD.
verses.20:6: I will add fifteen years to your days, and I will deliver you and this city from the grasp of the king of Assyria; and I will shield this city for My own sake and for the sake of My servant David.'"
verses.20:7: Then Isaiah said, "Take a cake of pressed figs." So they took one and laid it on the boil, and he recovered.
verses.20:8: Now Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "What is the sign that the LORD will heal me, and that I shall go up to the house of the LORD on the third day?"
verses.20:9: Isaiah said, "This is the sign for you from the LORD, that the LORD will carry out the word He has spoken: shall the shadow go forward ten steps, or shall it turn back ten steps?"
verses.20:10: Hezekiah said, "It is a simple thing for the shadow to lengthen ten steps; no, rather let the shadow turn backward ten steps."
verses.20:11: Then Isaiah the prophet called out to the LORD, and He caused the shadow to return backward ten steps along the steps by which it had descended on the steps of Ahaz.
verses.20:12: At that time Berodach-baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, for he had heard that Hezekiah had been sick.
verses.20:13: Hezekiah listened to them and showed them his entire treasure house—the silver, the gold, the spices, and the fine oil, along with his armory and all that was found in his storehouses. There was not a thing that Hezekiah did not show them in his house and in all his dominion.
verses.20:14: Then Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and said to him, "What did these men say, and from where have they come to you?" And Hezekiah said, "From a distant land they have come, from Babylon."
verses.20:15: He said, "What have they seen in your house?" And Hezekiah said, "All that is in my house they have seen; there was not a thing in my storehouses that I did not show them."
verses.20:16: Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, "Hear the word of the LORD:
verses.20:17: 'Look, days are coming when everything in your house, and all that your fathers have stored up until this day, will be carried away to Babylon; not a thing will be left,' says the LORD.
verses.20:18: 'And some of your sons who will come forth from you, whom you will father, will be taken away, and they will become eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.'"
verses.20:19: Then Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "Good is the word of the LORD that you have spoken." And he said, "Is it not so, if there will be peace and truth in my days?"
verses.20:20: As for the rest of the deeds of Hezekiah, all his might, and how he made the pool and the conduit and brought the water into the city, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.20:21: Then Hezekiah lay down with his fathers, and Manasseh his son became king in his place.
verses.21:1: Manasseh was twelve years old when he began reigning, and he reigned for fifty-five years in Jerusalem. The name of his mother was Hephzibah.
verses.21:2: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, following the abominations of the nations that the LORD had dispossessed from before the sons of Israel.
verses.21:3: He rebuilt the high places that his father Hezekiah had destroyed; he set up altars to Baal and made an Asherah, just as Ahab king of Israel had made, and he bowed down to all the host of the heavens and served them.
verses.21:4: He also built altars in the house of the LORD, concerning which the LORD had said, "In Jerusalem I will place My name."
verses.21:5: And he built altars for all the host of the heavens in the two courtyards of the house of the LORD.
verses.21:6: He made his son pass through the fire, practiced soothsaying and interpreted omens, and appointed a medium and spiritists. He did evil extensively in the eyes of the LORD, to provoke Him to anger.
verses.21:7: He placed the carved image of the Asherah that he had made inside the house about which the LORD had said to David and to his son Solomon, "In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will place My name forever.
verses.21:8: And I will not again cause the foot of Israel to wander from the land that I gave to their fathers, provided only that they are careful to act in keeping with all that I have commanded them, and with the whole law that My servant Moses commanded them."
verses.21:9: Yet they did not listen, and Manasseh led them astray to do more evil than the nations that the LORD had destroyed from before the sons of Israel.
verses.21:10: Then the LORD spoke by the hand of His servants the prophets, saying,
verses.21:11: "Because Manasseh, king of Judah, has done these abominations, acting more wickedly than all that the Amorites before him had done, and has also caused Judah to sin through his idols,
verses.21:12: therefore this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Look, I am bringing calamity upon Jerusalem and Judah, such that both ears of everyone who hears it will ring.
verses.21:13: I will stretch out over Jerusalem the measuring line of Samaria and the plumb line of the house of Ahab, and I will wipe Jerusalem just as someone wipes a dish, wiping it and turning it face down.
verses.21:14: I will forsake the remnant of My inheritance, giving them into the hand of their enemies, and they will become plunder and prey for all their enemies,
verses.21:15: because they have done what is evil in My eyes and have kept provoking Me to anger, from the day that their fathers came out of Egypt until this day."
verses.21:16: In addition, Manasseh shed innocent blood in great abundance, until he had filled Jerusalem from end to end, apart from his sin by which he caused Judah to sin, doing what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
verses.21:17: As for the rest of the deeds of Manasseh, and everything he did, and his sin that he sinned, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.21:18: Then Manasseh lay down with his fathers and was buried in the garden of his house, in the garden of Uzza; and his son Amon reigned in his place.
verses.21:19: Amon was twenty-two years old when he began reigning, and he reigned for two years in Jerusalem. The name of his mother was Meshullemeth, the daughter of Haruz, from Jotbah.
verses.21:20: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father Manasseh had done.
verses.21:21: He walked in the entire way that his father had walked; he served the idols that his father had served and bowed down to them.
verses.21:22: He abandoned the LORD, the God of his fathers, and he did not walk in the LORD's way.
verses.21:23: Amon's servants conspired against him and put the king to death inside his house.
verses.21:24: Then the people of the land struck down all the conspirators against King Amon, and the people of the land made his son Josiah king in his place.
verses.21:25: As for the rest of the deeds of Amon that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.21:26: They buried him in his tomb in the garden of Uzza, and his son Josiah reigned in his place.
verses.22:1: Josiah was eight years old when he began reigning, and he reigned for thirty-one years in Jerusalem. The name of his mother was Jedidah, the daughter of Adaiah, from Bozkath.
verses.22:2: He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, and he walked in the entire way of his father David, and did not turn aside to the right or left.
verses.22:3: Then in the eighteenth year of King Josiah, the king sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, son of Meshullam, the scribe, to the house of the LORD, saying,
verses.22:4: "Go up to Hilkiah the high priest so that he may sum up the silver brought into the house of the LORD, which the threshold keepers have gathered from the people.
verses.22:5: And let them give it into the hand of the workers who are appointed over the house of the LORD, and let them give it to the workers who are in the house of the LORD to repair the breaches of the house,
verses.22:6: to the craftsmen, the builders, and the masons, and for purchasing timber and quarried stone to repair the house.
verses.22:7: However, no reckoning shall be held with them for the silver given into their hand, because they act faithfully."
verses.22:8: Hilkiah the high priest said to Shaphan the scribe, "I have found the scroll of the law in the house of the LORD." Then Hilkiah gave the scroll to Shaphan, and he read it.
verses.22:9: Shaphan the scribe came to the king and brought word back to the king, and he said, "Your servants have poured out the silver found in the house and have given it into the hand of the workers who are appointed over the house of the LORD."
verses.22:10: Then Shaphan the scribe informed the king, saying, "Hilkiah the priest has given me a scroll." And Shaphan read it in the king's presence.
verses.22:11: When the king heard the words of the scroll of the law, he tore his garments.
verses.22:12: Then the king commanded Hilkiah the priest, and Ahikam son of Shaphan, and Achbor son of Micaiah, and Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah, the servant of the king, saying,
verses.22:13: "Go, inquire of the LORD on my behalf, on behalf of the people, and on behalf of all Judah, regarding the words of this scroll that has been found; for great is the LORD's wrath that has been kindled against us, because our fathers did not listen to the words of this scroll, to do according to everything written concerning us."
verses.22:14: So Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asaiah went to Huldah the prophetess, wife of Shallum son of Tikvah, son of Harhas, keeper of the garments—she was living in Jerusalem in the Second Quarter—and they spoke to her.
verses.22:15: She said to them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Say to the man who sent you to Me,
verses.22:16: 'This is what the LORD says: Look, I am bringing calamity upon this place and upon its inhabitants—all the words of the scroll that the king of Judah has read.
verses.22:17: Because they have forsaken Me and burned incense to other gods, so as to provoke Me to anger by all the work of their hands, My wrath will be kindled against this place, and it will not be extinguished.'
verses.22:18: But to the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of the LORD, say this to him: 'This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: As for the words that you have heard,
verses.22:19: because your heart softened and you humbled yourself before the LORD when you heard what I spoke against this place and against its inhabitants—that they would become a desolation and a curse—and you tore your garments and wept before Me, I too have heard, declares the LORD.
verses.22:20: Therefore, look, I am gathering you to your fathers, and you will be gathered to your burial place in peace; and your eyes will not look upon all the calamity that I am bringing on this place.'" Then they brought word back to the king.
verses.23:1: Then the king sent word, and they gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem to him.
verses.23:2: The king went up to the house of the LORD, and every man of Judah and all the residents of Jerusalem with him, along with the priests, the prophets, and all the people, from the smallest to the greatest. He read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant that had been found in the house of the LORD.
verses.23:3: Then the king stood beside the pillar and made the covenant before the LORD, to walk after the LORD and to keep His commandments, His testimonies, and His statutes with all the heart and all the soul, to uphold the words of this covenant that were written in this book. And all the people stood in the covenant.
verses.23:4: The king commanded Hilkiah the high priest, the priests of the second rank, and the keepers of the threshold to bring out from the temple of the LORD all the vessels made for Baal, for Asherah, and for all the host of heaven. He burned them outside Jerusalem in the fields of Kidron and carried their dust to Bethel.
verses.23:5: He did away with the idolatrous priests whom the kings of Judah had appointed, who burned incense at the high places in the cities of Judah and the surroundings of Jerusalem, along with those who burned incense to Baal, to the sun, to the moon, to the constellations, and to all the host of heaven.
verses.23:6: He brought the Asherah out from the house of the LORD, outside Jerusalem to the Brook Kidron, burned it at the Brook Kidron, crushed it to dust, and cast its dust over the grave of the common people.
verses.23:7: He tore down the houses of the male cult prostitutes that were in the house of the LORD, where the women were weaving tents for Asherah.
verses.23:8: He brought all the priests from the cities of Judah and defiled the high places where the priests had burned incense, from Geba to Beersheba. He also tore down the high places of the gates that were at the entrance of the gate of Joshua, the governor of the city, which were on a man's left at the gate of the city.
verses.23:9: Yet the priests of the high places did not ascend to the altar of the LORD in Jerusalem; instead, they ate unleavened bread in the midst of their brothers.
verses.23:10: He also defiled Topheth, which is in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, so that no one could cause his son or his daughter to pass through the fire to Molech.
verses.23:11: He did away with the horses that the kings of Judah had given to the sun, at the entrance of the house of the LORD, beside the chamber of Nathan-melech the court officer, which was in the precincts; and he burned the chariots of the sun with fire.
verses.23:12: The king tore down the altars that were on the roof of the upper chamber of Ahaz, which the kings of Judah had made, along with the altars that Manasseh had made in the two courts of the house of the LORD; he crushed them away from there and cast their dust into the Brook Kidron.
verses.23:13: The king also defiled the high places that were east of Jerusalem, south of the Mount of Destruction, which Solomon king of Israel had built for Ashtoreth the detestable thing of the Sidonians, for Chemosh the detestable thing of Moab, and for Milcom the abomination of the sons of Ammon.
verses.23:14: He shattered the standing stones, cut down the Asherim, and filled their place with human bones.
verses.23:15: Furthermore, the altar that was at Bethel, the high place that Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, had made—he tore down both that altar and the high place; he burned the high place, crushed it to dust, and burned an Asherah.
verses.23:16: Then Josiah turned and saw the graves that were there on the mountain, and he sent and took the bones from the graves and burned them on the altar and defiled it, according to the word of the LORD that the man of God had proclaimed, who proclaimed these things.
verses.23:17: Then he said, "What is that monument that I see?" And the men of the city said to him, "It is the grave of the man of God who came from Judah and proclaimed these things that you have done against the altar of Bethel."
verses.23:18: He said, "Leave him alone; let no man move his bones." So they spared his bones, together with the bones of the prophet who came from Samaria.
verses.23:19: Josiah also removed all the houses of the high places that were in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had made to provoke anger, and he did to them according to all the deeds that he had done at Bethel.
verses.23:20: He slaughtered all the priests of the high places who were there on the altars and burned human bones upon them. Then he returned to Jerusalem.
verses.23:21: Then the king commanded all the people, saying, "Observe Passover to the LORD your God, as is written in this book of the covenant."
verses.23:22: For no Passover like this had been observed since the days of the judges who judged Israel, nor in all the days of the kings of Israel and the kings of Judah.
verses.23:23: Instead, in the eighteenth year of King Josiah, this Passover was observed to the LORD in Jerusalem.
verses.23:24: Moreover, Josiah purged the mediums and the spiritists, the household gods, the idols, and all the detestable things that were seen in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, in order to uphold the words of the law that were written in the book that Hilkiah the priest had found in the house of the LORD.
verses.23:25: No king before him was like him, who turned back to the LORD with all his heart, all his soul, and all his strength, according to the entire law of Moses; and after him no one like him arose.
verses.23:26: Still, the LORD did not turn back from the heat of His great anger, with which His anger burned against Judah, because of all the provocations with which Manasseh had provoked Him.
verses.23:27: And the LORD said, "I will remove Judah also from My presence, just as I removed Israel, and I will reject this city that I have chosen, Jerusalem, and the house of which I said, 'My name will be there.'"
verses.23:28: As for the rest of the acts of Josiah and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.23:29: In his days, Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt went up to the king of Assyria by the Euphrates River. King Josiah went to meet him, and he put him to death at Megiddo when he saw him.
verses.23:30: His servants carried him dead by chariot from Megiddo, brought him to Jerusalem, and buried him in his tomb. Then the people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah, anointed him, and made him king in place of his father.
verses.23:31: Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.
verses.23:32: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that his fathers had done.
verses.23:33: Pharaoh Neco put him in bonds at Riblah in the land of Hamath so that he would not reign in Jerusalem, and he imposed on the land a fine of one hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold.
verses.23:34: Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim son of Josiah king in place of Josiah his father, and changed his name to Jehoiakim. But he took Jehoahaz, and he went to Egypt and died there.
verses.23:35: Jehoiakim gave the silver and the gold to Pharaoh, yet he assessed the land to give the silver at Pharaoh's command. He exacted the silver and the gold from the people of the land, each man according to his assessment, to give to Pharaoh Neco.
verses.23:36: Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zebudah daughter of Pedaiah from Rumah.
verses.23:37: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that his fathers had done.
verses.24:1: In his days, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his servant for three years; then he turned and rebelled against him.
verses.24:2: The LORD sent against him raiding bands of Chaldeans, raiding bands of Aram, raiding bands of Moab, and raiding bands of the sons of Ammon; He sent them against Judah to destroy it, according to the word of the LORD that He had spoken by the hand of His servants the prophets.
verses.24:3: Indeed, this came upon Judah at the command of the LORD, to remove them from His presence because of the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he had done,
verses.24:4: and also because of the blood of the innocent that he had shed, for he filled Jerusalem with innocent blood; and the LORD was not willing to forgive.
verses.24:5: As for the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.24:6: So Jehoiakim lay down with his fathers, and Jehoiachin his son became king in his place.
verses.24:7: And the king of Egypt did not go out of his land again, for the king of Babylon had taken everything that had belonged to the king of Egypt, from the Brook of Egypt to the Euphrates River.
verses.24:8: Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Nehushta daughter of Elnathan from Jerusalem.
verses.24:9: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that his father had done.
verses.24:10: At that time, the servants of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up to Jerusalem, and the city came under siege.
verses.24:11: Then Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to the city while his servants were besieging it.
verses.24:12: Then Jehoiachin king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon—he, his mother, his servants, his officials, and his court officers. And the king of Babylon took him in the eighth year of his reign.
verses.24:13: He brought out from there all the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the house of the king, and he cut in pieces all the vessels of gold that Solomon king of Israel had made in the temple of the LORD, just as the LORD had spoken.
verses.24:14: He carried into exile all Jerusalem, all the officials, and all the mighty men of valor—ten thousand exiles—along with all the artisans and the smiths. No one was left except the poorest of the people of the land.
verses.24:15: He carried Jehoiachin into exile to Babylon; and the king's mother, the king's wives, his court officers, and the leading men of the land he led into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.
verses.24:16: All the men of valor, seven thousand, and the artisans and the smiths, one thousand—all of them mighty men who waged war—the king of Babylon brought them into exile to Babylon.
verses.24:17: Then the king of Babylon made Mattaniah, his uncle, king in his place, and changed his name to Zedekiah.
verses.24:18: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.
verses.24:19: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.
verses.24:20: For on account of the anger of the LORD, this happened in Jerusalem and in Judah until He cast them away from His presence. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.
verses.25:1: It happened in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month, that Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came, he and all his army, against Jerusalem. He camped against it, and they built a siege wall against it all around.
verses.25:2: Thus the city came under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
verses.25:3: On the ninth of the month, the famine grew severe in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.
verses.25:4: Then the city was breached, and all the men of war went out at night by way of the gate between the two walls, which was by the king's garden, while the Chaldeans were against the city all around; and he went along the road to the Arabah.
verses.25:5: The army of the Chaldeans pursued after the king, and they overtook him in the plains of Jericho, and all his army dispersed away from him.
verses.25:6: They seized the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon, to Riblah, and they pronounced judgment on him.
verses.25:7: They slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes; then he blinded the eyes of Zedekiah, bound him in bronze shackles, and brought him to Babylon.
verses.25:8: Now in the fifth month, on the seventh of the month—this was the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon—Nebuzaradan, chief of the bodyguard, servant of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
verses.25:9: He burned the house of the LORD and the house of the king, and all the houses of Jerusalem and every great house he burned with fire.
verses.25:11: And Nebuzaradan, chief of the bodyguard, took into exile the rest of the people who were left in the city, the defectors who had defected to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude.
verses.25:12: But of the poorest of the land, the chief of the bodyguard left some as vinedressers and farmers.
verses.25:13: And the Chaldeans smashed to pieces the bronze pillars that were in the house of the LORD, and the stands and the bronze sea that were in the house of the LORD, and they carried their bronze to Babylon.
verses.25:14: They took the pots, the shovels, the snuffers, the ladles, and all the bronze articles with which they used to minister.
verses.25:15: And the chief of the bodyguard took the firepans and the sprinkling bowls—whatever was gold as gold, and whatever was silver as silver.
verses.25:16: As for the two pillars, the one sea, and the stands that Solomon had made for the house of the LORD, the bronze of all these articles could not be weighed.
verses.25:17: Eighteen cubits was the height of the one pillar, and a bronze capital was on top of it; the height of the capital was three cubits, and latticework and pomegranates were on the capital all around, all of it bronze. And things like these were on the second pillar, along with the latticework.
verses.25:18: Then the chief of the bodyguard took Seraiah, the chief priest, and Zephaniah, the priest of second rank, and the three threshold keepers.
verses.25:19: And from the city he took one official who was an overseer over the men of war; five men from those who saw the king's face, who were found in the city; the scribe, the commander of the army, who mustered the people of the land; and sixty men from the people of the land who were found in the city.
verses.25:20: Nebuzaradan, chief of the bodyguard, took them and led them to the king of Babylon, to Riblah.
verses.25:21: Then the king of Babylon struck them down and killed them in Riblah, in the land of Hamath. Thus Judah went into exile from its soil.
verses.25:22: And over the people who were left in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, had left, he appointed Gedaliah, son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan.
verses.25:23: When all the commanders of the forces, they and the men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah, they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah—Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite, they and their men.
verses.25:24: And Gedaliah swore to them and to their men, and he said to them, "Do not fear the servants of the Chaldeans; reside in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will be good for you."
verses.25:25: And it happened in the seventh month that Ishmael, son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, of the royal seed, came with ten men, and they struck down Gedaliah—and he died—as well as the Judeans and the Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.
verses.25:26: Then all the people, from small to great, along with the commanders of the forces, rose up and went into Egypt, for they feared the Chaldeans.
verses.25:27: And it happened in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin, king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh of the month, that Evil-merodach, king of Babylon, in the year he became king, lifted up the head of Jehoiachin, king of Judah, out of prison.
verses.25:28: He spoke kind words with him and placed his throne above the throne of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
verses.25:29: He changed his prison garments, and he ate bread continually in his presence all the days of his life.
verses.25:30: And his provision—a continual provision—was given to him from the king, each day's portion on its day, all the days of his life.

notes.1:3: The rhetorical question uses an emphatic double negative, literally 'from without there is not God in Israel,' underscoring the offense of consulting Ekron's god; the same construction recurs in 1:6 and 1:16.
notes.1:7: The Hebrew noun mishpat ('judgment, custom, manner') here refers to the man's characteristic appearance and bearing.
notes.1:8: Literally 'a man, possessor of hair,' which may indicate either a physically hairy man or one wearing a coarse garment of hair.
notes.1:15: The form oto here represents the preposition 'with' plus suffix (normally itto), a spelling common in Kings that recurs in 3:12 and 3:26.
notes.2:8: The verb wayyiglom ('folded it up,' Qal of glm) is a biblical hapax legomenon.
notes.2:9: Literally 'a portion of two' (pi-shenayim), the legal idiom for the firstborn's double share of an inheritance (cf. Deut 21:17), marking Elisha's request to succeed Elijah as primary heir.
notes.2:10: The passive participle luqqach ('being taken') lacks the usual mem- prefix of a Pual participle, or represents a Qal passive participle.
notes.2:14: Following the Masoretic punctuation (atnah on 'Elijah'), aph-hu ('he too') introduces the resumed clause describing Elisha's striking of the water; some read it with the preceding question as 'even He?'
notes.2:16: Ketiv/Qere orthographic variant: the Qere reads haggeyayot (standard plural of gay, 'valleys'), whereas the Ketiv omits the consonantal yod (hgywt), with the same meaning.
notes.3:16: The Qal infinitive absolute asoh functions as an imperative ('Make'), and the doubled noun gevim gevim ('trenches, trenches') expresses distribution ('full of trenches').
notes.3:23: The phrase pairs a Hophal infinitive absolute (hochorev) with a Niphal perfect (nechervu) of chrb ('fight, lay waste') for strong emphasis ('have surely destroyed one another').
notes.3:24: Ketiv/Qere variant: the Qere reads wayyakku-vah ('and they struck into it,' referring to Moab's territory), followed by the continuing Hiphil infinitive wehakkot ('continuing to strike'); the Ketiv wybw reads 'and they entered into it.'
notes.3:25: The clause ad-hish'ir avaneyha baqqir chareset is compressed, literally 'until leaving its stones in Kir-hareseth,' indicating that the devastation left only the stonework of Kir-hareseth standing.
notes.3:27: Hebrew qetseph-gadol ('great wrath') does not specify the source of the wrath in the text, leaving open whether it denotes divine displeasure or fierce Moabite fury.
notes.4:2: The ketiv preserves the archaic second-person feminine singular pronominal suffix -ki (also in vv. 3 and 7, along with archaic feminine singular pronoun and verb forms in vv. 16 and 23), while the qere reads the standard Masoretic form; the translation follows the qere. The rare noun translated 'flask' (asuk) is a hapax legomenon derived from the root 'to anoint.'
notes.4:5: For 'kept pouring,' the ketiv writes a I-yod Hiphil feminine participle while the qere reads the pausal I-waw Hiphil feminine participle (motsaqet); both have the same active meaning.
notes.4:13: Literally 'you have trembled toward us with all this trembling,' a Qal verb with its cognate noun expressing attentive, anxious care.
notes.4:16: The Hebrew idiom literally means 'according to a living time,' referring to the return of the same season in the following year (cf. Gen 18:10, 14).
notes.4:42: The noun translated 'sack' (tsiqelon) is a hapax legomenon, traditionally understood as a bag or pouch, though some modern scholars interpret it as a husk or sheath.
notes.5:1: Hebrew tsara'at ('leprosy,' with the Pual participle metsora', 'leprous') designates a range of serious, ritually defiling skin afflictions rather than solely modern Hansen's disease.
notes.5:3: The verb translated 'cure' here and in vv. 6, 7, and 11 is Qal asaph ('gather in, remove'), used idiomatically for removing leprosy and restoring the afflicted person to the community.
notes.5:12: The translation follows the qere reading 'Amanah' rather than the ketiv 'Abana,' reflecting a known interchange of b and m in the river's ancient names.
notes.5:18: In the second petition, the particle na ('please') is written in the ketiv but omitted in the qere (a ketiv velo qere); the translation follows the qere.
notes.5:25: For 'Where have you come from,' the ketiv writes a contracted spelling while the qere reads the standard interrogative me'ayin ('from where'), with identical meaning.
notes.6:5: Hebrew literally reads 'the iron,' referring to the iron ax head, and places the particle et before the subject of the intransitive verb nafal, a syntactic usage attested occasionally in Kings.
notes.6:6: The verb wayyatsef is the Hiphil of tsuf ('to float'), translated causatively here ('caused the iron to float'), though it can also be taken intransitively ('the iron floated').
notes.6:22: The Masoretic Text frames a rhetorical 'how much less' question — you would not strike down even captives taken with your own weapons — without the negative particle supplied by some ancient versions.
notes.6:25: Following the euphemistic qere div-yonim ('droppings/discharge of doves') rather than the cruder ketiv chirei-yonim ('dung of doves'); some identify the expression as a colloquial name for a wild plant or seed pods.
notes.6:27: Hebrew al-yoshi'ekh is literally a negated jussive ('May the LORD not help you'), functioning idiomatically here as a negative conditional protasis ('If the LORD does not help you').
notes.7:4: Hebrew literally says 'let us fall to the camp of Aram,' a standard military idiom for deserting or surrendering to an enemy.
notes.7:12: Following the qere bassadeh ('in the field') rather than the ketiv bahassadeh, which retains an unelided definite article; both carry the same meaning.
notes.7:13: Following the qere hamon ('multitude,' standard construct state) rather than the ketiv hahamon, which retains an anomalous definite article in construct; the Masoretic Text preserves both parallel clauses comparing the horses' fate to that of all Israel.
notes.7:15: Following the qere bechofzam (Qal infinitive construct of chafaz, 'in their haste') rather than the ketiv behechafzam (Niphal infinitive construct, 'in their panicked flight').
notes.7:18: Hebrew wayehi kedabber uses a temporal Piel infinitive construct ('when the man of God had spoken') whose main clause follows in verse 19; the order of barley and fine flour is reversed here from verse 1.
notes.8:10: The Qere reads 'to him' (lo), matching Hazael's report in v. 14; the Ketiv reads 'not' (lo), which would yield 'Go, say, "You will surely not recover."' Both 'surely recover' and 'surely die' translate emphatic infinitive absolutes.
notes.8:11: Literally 'he made his face stand and set [it] until being ashamed,' an idiom for staring fixedly to an awkward or embarrassing extent; Hebrew leaves unspecified whether Hazael or Elisha felt the discomfort.
notes.8:15: The Hebrew noun makber ('bedcover') occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible and denotes a thick woven cloth or netting.
notes.8:16: The Masoretic text retains the circumstantial clause 'while Jehoshaphat was king of Judah,' indicating a coregency between Jehoshaphat and his son Jehoram.
notes.9:4: The Masoretic text repeats the noun hanna'ar ('the young man'), accented to read 'the young man, the young prophet' or 'the young man, the prophet's attendant.'
notes.9:8: 'Every male' renders the vivid Hebrew idiom mashtin beqir (literally 'one who urinates against a wall'); 'both bound and free' (atsur we'azuv, literally 'restrained and let go') is a merism encompassing every category of person.
notes.9:13: 'The bare steps' translates gerem hamma'alot, literally 'the bone/structure of the steps,' meaning either the bare steps themselves or the top landing of the stairway.
notes.9:23: Literally 'turned his hands,' a chariot-driving idiom for pulling the reins to wheel around.
notes.9:27: The Masoretic text moves straight from Jehu's command at the ascent of Gur to Ahaziah's flight to Megiddo without an explicit clause stating the blow's execution, whereas the Septuagint adds 'and they struck him.'
notes.10:1: The Masoretic Hebrew reads "the officials of Jezreel" (rather than Samaria, as in some ancient versions) and literally "the guardians of Ahab," referring to the guardians entrusted with raising Ahab's sons.
notes.10:12: The Masoretic Hebrew uses three consecutive wayyiqtol verbs ("arose and came and went"), and "Beth-eked of the Shepherds" literally means "house of binding of the shepherds," likely a sheep-shearing station along the road.
notes.10:15: Masoretic vocalization and cantillation pair the repeated affirmative particle ("yesh wa-yesh," rendered "It is, indeed it is!") as Jehonadab's emphatic reply, followed directly by Jehu's command without an explicit speaker-change clause.
notes.10:25: "Citadel" translates Hebrew "ir" (literally "city"), here denoting the walled inner precinct or stronghold within the temple complex of Baal.
notes.10:27: The Ketiv reads a noun from the root for dung/excrement ("dunghills/outhouses"), while the Masoretic Qere euphemistically substitutes "motsa'ot" (literally "places of going out," i.e., a latrine), which is followed here.
notes.11:2: The Qere reads the Hophal participle ("who were being put to death") for the irregular Ketiv form; the Hebrew also places "him and his nurse, into the bedroom" directly after "stole him away" without an additional verb and shifts to the plural Hiphil verb "they hid him."
notes.11:4: The Qere reads "hundreds" ("me'ot") for the unusual Ketiv spelling ("me'iyot"), an orthographic Ketiv/Qere variant that recurs in 11:9, 10, and 15.
notes.11:6: "As a barrier" renders the Hebrew hapax legomenon "massah" (from a root meaning "to pull or ward off"), denoting defense against intrusion; "coming in on the Sabbath" (11:5) and "going out on the Sabbath" (11:7) are idioms for guard shifts rotating on and off duty.
notes.11:15: The Hebrew phrase "el-mibbayit la-sederot" literally means "inside/between the ranks," depicting Athaliah being escorted out between the lines of armed guards.
notes.11:16: The Hebrew idiom literally reads "they placed hands for her," understood either as seizing her ("they laid hands on her") or as parting to make way for her to exit the temple precinct.
notes.12:5: Hebrew kesef 'over ('current silver,' cf. Gen 23:16) can also be read as 'silver of one passing over' in the census (cf. Exod 30:13). Hebrew kesef nafshot 'erko literally means 'silver of persons of his valuation' (cf. Lev 27:2-8).
notes.12:10: Following the Qere ('on the right side,' lit. 'from the right'); the Ketiv uses the preposition 'in/at' rather than 'from' before 'right.'
notes.12:12: Following the pointed Qere reading 'into the hands of' (plural construct, against a singular variant 'hand of') and the Qere Hophal participle 'those placed in charge' (against the Ketiv 'the overseers/appointed ones').
notes.12:13: Hebrew lechozqah is a feminine noun with preposition meaning 'for repair/strengthening' (not a suffix 'her').
notes.12:21: Hebrew hayyored Silla literally reads 'the one going down to Silla' (Qal active participle), likely referring to the road or descent leading down toward Silla.
notes.13:2: Hebrew mimmennah ('from it,' feminine singular) refers collectively to the plural noun 'sins' (likewise bah, 'in it,' in 13:6 and 13:11).
notes.13:6: The Masoretic Text shifts from plural 'they did not turn aside' (saru) to masculine singular 'he walked' (halakh), referring either to King Jehoahaz or to Israel collectively.
notes.13:7: Hebrew lo hish'ir is an active Hiphil 3ms verb ('did not leave') without an explicit subject, translated impersonally here ('no troops had been left'), though the unexpressed subject may be the LORD or the king of Aram.
notes.13:19: Hebrew lehakkot ('to strike,' Hiphil infinitive construct with the preposition l-) expresses past obligation here: 'You ought to have struck.'
notes.13:20: Hebrew ba shanah (lit. 'coming of a year' or 'a year came') is a concise idiom meaning at the turn or beginning of the year, when military campaigning resumed in spring.
notes.14:2: The Qere (read form) is Jehoaddan, whereas the Ketiv (written form) reads Jehoaddin.
notes.14:6: The Qere reads the Hophal imperfect "shall be put to death" (matching Deut 24:16), whereas the Ketiv reads the Qal imperfect "shall die."
notes.14:13: The Qere reads the singular "he came," whereas the Ketiv reads the plural "they came."
notes.14:26: Hebrew moreh ("bitter") resembles the participle of marah ("rebellious") but is widely understood in context as a variant for "bitter." The paired passive participles "bond" and "free" (literally "confined" and "released") form a merism for all classes of people.
notes.14:28: The Masoretic Hebrew literally reads "for Judah in Israel," a difficult phrase often understood as territories formerly belonging to Judah now restored to Israel.
notes.15:5: Hebrew beth hachophshith ("a separate house") literally denotes a house of exemption or isolation, referring to royal quarantine quarters.
notes.15:10: The Masoretic Hebrew reads qobol-am ("in front of the people," i.e., publicly), using a rare preposition related to Aramaic qobel ("before").
notes.15:13: The Hebrew text alternates between Azariah (vv. 1, 6, 7, 8, 17, 23, 27) and Uzziah (vv. 13, 30, 32, 34) for the same Judean king.
notes.15:20: Hebrew gibbore hachayil literally means "mighty men of strength/substance," referring here to wealthy men of standing.
notes.15:25: The Hebrew particle eth before Argob and Arieh (literally "the Lion") is ambiguous, meaning either that Pekah struck them down alongside Pekahiah or that they joined him in the assassination. The Qere reads "the king" with the definite article, whereas the Ketiv omits it.
notes.16:6: Ketiv reads "and Arameans" (w'rmym), while Qere reads "and Edomites" (wa'edomim), which is followed here. Earlier in the verse the Masoretic Text reads "to Aram," reflecting the graphical similarity of dalet and resh in Hebrew.
notes.16:14: The verb rendered "moved" (wayyaqrev) is the Hiphil of q-r-v, literally "brought near" or "brought forward," resuming the fronted direct object ("the bronze altar") to describe relocating it from the temple front to the north side of the new altar.
notes.16:15: Qere reads the Piel wayyiqtol waytsawweh ("commanded") without an object suffix, whereas Ketiv adds a proleptic third-person masculine singular suffix ("commanded him"). The Piel infinitive levaqqer ("for inquiry") denotes examining, deliberating, or seeking an oracle.
notes.16:18: Qere reads musakh (Ketiv mysk), a hapax legomenon generally derived from s-k-kh ("cover") meaning a covered structure or canopy. The Hiphil verb hesev (from s-v-v, "turn aside, shift, divert") with "house of the LORD" as an adverbial accusative indicates that Ahaz relocated or altered these structures at the temple.
notes.17:9: The verb rendered "did in secret" (waychappe'u) is a hapax legomenon, the Piel of ch-p-' (a byform of ch-p-h, "cover, conceal"), expressing covert or disguised conduct.
notes.17:13: Qere reads the plural construct form nevi'e ("all the prophets, every seer"), whereas Ketiv reads nvy'w ("His prophet" or "His prophets").
notes.17:21: Because Qal qara ("tore") is transitive in Biblical Hebrew, the LORD (from v. 20) is its implied subject and "Israel" its object. For the following verb, Qere reads wayyaddach (Hiphil of n-d-ch, "drove away"), whereas Ketiv reads wyd' (from the rare byform n-d-').
notes.17:27: The Masoretic Text shifts from singular "one of the priests" to plural jussives ("let them go and live there," likely encompassing the priest together with his household or escorts) before returning to singular ("let him teach them").
notes.17:31: Qere reads elohe ("gods of") and Sepharvayim ("Sepharvaim"), whereas Ketiv writes 'lh and sprym respectively.
notes.18:16: The Hebrew verb qissas (Piel, cut off or stripped) takes the doors and the rare term omenot (doorposts or supports, appearing only here in the Hebrew Bible) as direct objects without explicitly naming gold, though stripping the metal plating is implied by had overlaid (sippah, Piel).
notes.18:20: The opening clause is elliptical in Hebrew, literally "You say—only a word of lips—counsel and might for the war," with the second-person Qal perfect amarta (whereas the parallel in Isaiah 36:5 reads first-person "I say").
notes.18:27: The translation follows the Masoretic Qere readings "their excrement" (soatam) and "the water of their feet" (meme raglehem), polite euphemisms read in place of the plainer written Ketiv forms "their dung" (harehem) and "their urine" (shenehem).
notes.18:29: The Masoretic Text literally reads "from his hand" (third-person reference to the king of Assyria, matching "This is what the king says"), whereas some ancient versions read "from my hand" and the parallel in Isaiah 36:14 omits the prepositional phrase.
notes.18:31: Literally "Make a blessing with me" (asu-itti berakah), a Hebrew diplomatic idiom for coming to terms of peace or presenting a tribute of submission.
notes.19:14: Hebrew uses the plural noun hassepharim ("letters/documents") and plural object suffix in wayyiqra'em ("read them") for a single official dispatch, then shifts to the singular suffix in wayyiphresehu ("spread it out").
notes.19:23: Ketiv brkb ("with the chariotry of") vs. Qere berob ("with the multitude of"), which is followed here and matches Isaiah 37:24.
notes.19:24: Hebrew Masor is a poetic designation for Egypt (cognate with Akkadian Musur; cf. Isaiah 19:6; 37:25; Micah 7:12), paired with ye'ore ("Nile streams/channels"), though homonymous with the noun meaning "siege" or "fortress."
notes.19:31: In the Masoretic Text, seba'ot ("of hosts") is a Qere without Ketiv, read aloud in the Masoretic tradition though absent from the consonantal text (cf. Isaiah 37:32).
notes.19:37: In the Masoretic Text, banaw ("his sons") is a Qere without Ketiv, read according to the Masoretic tradition though absent from the consonantal text (cf. Isaiah 37:38).
notes.20:4: Ketiv h'yr ("the city") vs. Qere haser ("courtyard"), which is followed here ("the middle courtyard").
notes.20:11: The verb yaredah ("had descended") is feminine singular despite the masculine noun hassel ("the shadow"), likely pointing implicitly to the sun (hassemes, feminine; cf. Isaiah 38:8).
notes.20:13: The Masoretic Text reads wayyisma' ("listened," Qal of sm'), whereas Isaiah 39:2 has wayyismah ("rejoiced"); bet nekotoh ("his treasure house") reflects an Akkadian loanword (bit nakamti) with an archaic 3ms suffix.
notes.20:18: Ketiv yqh (3ms singular) vs. Qere yiqqahu (Qal imperfect 3mp in pause of lqh, with indefinite plural subject rendered passively as "will be taken away," cf. Isaiah 39:7).
notes.20:19: Hebrew halo' 'im ("is it not, if...") is elliptical, resuming tob ("good") from the preceding clause ("Is it not so/good, if...").
notes.21:6: The Qal verb 'asah ('made' or 'appointed') with singular 'ov ('medium' or 'necromantic spirit') and plural yidde'onim ('spiritists') refers to instituting or consulting practitioners of necromancy and spiritism.
notes.21:12: The qere reads shom'ah ('everyone who hears it,' Qal participle with a feminine singular suffix referring back to 'calamity'); the ketiv writes sh-m-'-y-w, likely anticipating the ending of 'his ears.'
notes.21:16: The phrase 'from end to end' renders the literal Hebrew idiom 'mouth to mouth,' meaning filled to the brim or throughout the entire city (cf. 2 Kings 10:21; Ezra 9:11).
notes.21:26: The Masoretic verb is third-person masculine singular Qal active ('one buried him,' functioning impersonally as 'they buried him' or 'he was buried'), contrasting with the Niphal passive used for Manasseh in 21:18.
notes.22:4: The verb 'sum up' renders the Hiphil jussive of tamam ('make complete,' here to finish tallying or total the collected silver).
notes.22:5: Two ketiv/qere variants occur here: first, the qere reads weyittenuhu ('and let them give it,' third-person plural), while the ketiv writes w-y-t-n-h (singular or defective); second, the qere omits the preposition before 'the house of the LORD' (matching v. 9), whereas the ketiv reads 'in the house of the LORD.'
notes.22:9: The verb 'poured out' is the Hiphil perfect of natak ('pour out' or 'melt down'), referring to emptying the accumulated silver from the temple chest (or melting it for weighing) to pay the workers.
notes.22:14: 'The Second Quarter' translates ha-mishneh (literally 'the Second'), designating the newer expanded district of Jerusalem (cf. Zephaniah 1:10).
notes.22:15: Syntactically, 'to Me' stands inside the LORD's speech introduced by 'This is what the LORD says,' paralleling 'to inquire of the LORD' in v. 18, though some interpreters take it as Huldah speaking in her own voice ('to me').
notes.23:5: MT has the 3ms Piel wayyiqtol wayqatter ('and he burned incense'), understood distributively of the appointed priests. Hebrew mazzalot ('constellations') is a hapax legomenon denoting celestial bodies or zodiac constellations.
notes.23:7: Hebrew battim literally means 'houses'; as the object of the Qal participle oregot ('weaving'), it refers to woven tent-shrines, canopies, or hangings made for Asherah.
notes.23:10: Following the Qere ben-hinnom ('son of Hinnom'); the Ketiv reads the plural bene-hinnom ('sons of Hinnom').
notes.23:12: Hebrew wayyarots mishsham is formally ambiguous: it may be a Qal wayyiqtol of ratsats ('crush/smash') in a pregnant construction ('crushed and removed them from there'), or a Qal wayyiqtol of ruts ('he ran/hurried from there').
notes.23:29: The preposition al before 'the king of Assyria' is rendered 'to' (as often in later Kings, cf. 24:12), reflecting Pharaoh Neco's march to aid Assyria rather than to oppose it.
notes.23:33: Following the Qere mimmelok ('from reigning', i.e., so that he would not reign); the Ketiv reads bimlok ('while reigning').
notes.24:10: Following the Qere plural alu ('came up'), agreeing with the plural subject 'servants'; the Ketiv reads the 3ms singular alah.
notes.24:14: Following the Qere construct aseret before 'thousands' ('ten thousand'); the Ketiv reads the absolute form asarah. Hebrew goleh is a collective Qal active participle ('exiles').
notes.24:15: Following the Qere ele ('leading men', literally 'rams', used metaphorically for prominent leaders); the Ketiv reads the variant form ule.
notes.25:3: The Masoretic Hebrew reads simply 'on the ninth of the month,' without naming the month; compare the parallel account in Jeremiah 52:6, which specifies the fourth month.
notes.25:4: The Hebrew omits a verb of motion after 'all the men of war' (supplied here as 'went out' for readability; compare Jeremiah 52:7) and uses a singular Qal verb 'and he went' at the end, referring to King Zedekiah.
notes.25:15: The terse Hebrew phrasing literally reads 'what was gold, gold, and what was silver, silver,' indicating either items taken for their bullion value or items made of pure gold and pure silver.
notes.25:17: The written ketiv has the singular ammah ('cubit'), whereas the read qere translated here has the plural ammot ('cubits'), agreeing with the numeral 'three.'
notes.25:27: 'Lifted up the head of' is a Hebrew idiom meaning to show royal favor, restore to honor, and grant release from prison.

unplaced.text: And the whole army of the Chaldeans who were with the commander of the guard tore down the walls of Jerusalem all around.
unplaced.note: The Masoretic Text omits a preposition before "commander of the guard," reading literally "who the commander of the guard."
